question: Who is under obligation to be familiar with the traffic laws and obey them?
answers: Only a pedestrian
Every road user.
Only a professional driver.
Only a driver.
explanation: Traffic law obligates every person using the road—drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and passengers alike—to know and follow the traffic rules, not drivers alone.

question: Under what conditions can a person drive a motor vehicle?
answers: The driver must have a valid license for the same class of vehicle.
According to the conditions, laid down in the annual test.
The driver should be the registered owner or have legal control.
According to the conditions laid down in the Manufacturer’s manual.
explanation: A person may only drive a motor vehicle if they hold a valid driver's license issued for that specific vehicle class; the license-class match is the legal precondition for driving.

question: What is the duty of a person who owns or has control of a vehicle?
answers: Not to permit to anyone to drive, who doesn’t have a valid license for the type of vehicle.
To register any person who drives his vehicle in the vehicle travel log
To allow any person who asks him to drive his vehicle.
To make sure that photocopies of the driver’s license and insurance policy only are carried in the vehicle
explanation: The owner or person controlling a vehicle has a legal duty to prevent anyone from driving it who lacks a valid license for that type of vehicle, since the owner is responsible for who takes the wheel.

question: Apart from a driving instructor, who may escort a “new driver”?
answers: Any holder of a valid driving license for the same class of vehicle, and aged at least 24 yrs old.
A holder of a driving license for the same class of vehicle for at least 3 years and aged at least 30 yrs old, or a holder of a license for at least 2 yrs and aged at least 35 yrs old.
Any person who has not been convicted for any traffic offence during the past two years.
A holder of a driving license for the same class of vehicle for at least 5 years and aged at least 24 yrs old, or a holder of a license for at least 3 yrs and aged at least 30 yrs old.
explanation: Regulation sets two alternative experience-and-age thresholds for a lawful escort: a same-class license held for at least five years with the escort aged 24 or over, or held for at least three years with the escort aged 30 or over.

question: Is a policeman allowed to detain without a warrant a driver who committed an offence in front of him?
answers: Not under any condition
Yes, but only under a court certificate
Yes, if the driver doesn’t give his name and address or doesn’t present his license as required
Yes, only if the driver committed an offence that actually endangered road users
explanation: A police officer may detain a driver without a warrant specifically when the driver fails to give their name and address or refuses to present their license as legally required, since identification is the officer's basis for proceeding.

question: A police officer may revoke a driver’s license for a period of thirty days:
answers: When the driver endangers the life of a person on a pedestrian crossing
An arrest warrant was issued against the vehicle’s owner
When the driver committed an offence of holding a driver’s license that has been expired for more than ten days
When the passenger on the driver’s side did not wear a seatbelt
explanation: A 30-day license revocation applies when a driver's conduct endangers a person on a pedestrian crossing, reflecting the extra legal protection given to pedestrians at crossings.

question: A police officer may revoke a driver’s license for a period of sixty days:
answers: When the driver commits a traffic offence which doesn’t cause a road accident
When a driver involved in an accident is reasonably suspected of being responsible for causing injury or causing damage to property.
When the driver is caught speeding
When the driver commits a traffic offence in which a person is killed
explanation: A 60-day revocation is triggered when a driver involved in an accident is reasonably suspected of causing injury to a person or damage to property, a lower threshold than proof of guilt but enough for immediate precaution.

question: When may a police officer revoke a driver’s license for a period of ninety days?
answers: When the driver is involved in a car accident in which only property damage was caused
When the driver disobeys a stop sign
When a driver involved in an accident is reasonably suspected of causing the death of a person.
When the driver fails to give right of way.
explanation: The most severe 90-day revocation applies when a driver involved in an accident is reasonably suspected of causing a person's death, reflecting the seriousness of a fatal outcome.

question: What is the penalty for driving whilst disqualified?
answers: A fine of 80,000 NIS
6 yrs in jail and 2 yrs on probation.
None, if the driver presents a valid driver’s license within 7 days
Up to 3 years in jail, plus other penalties.
explanation: Driving while disqualified is treated as a serious offense under traffic law, carrying up to three years imprisonment in addition to other penalties, because it defies a formal order removing driving privileges.

question: What is the legal definition of a “road”
answers: Any place that is open for public passage, except for city streets
Asphalt or concrete paved road ways only.
The term “road” has no legal definition
Any rail, street, alley, square, passage, bridge and any other open space in which the public has a right to pass through
explanation: The legal definition of a road is deliberately broad, covering any rail, street, alley, square, passage, or bridge where the public has a right to pass, not only paved city streets.

question: What is the legal definition of “lighting up time”
answers: The time period of natural lighting conditions, when there is no need to have the vehicle lights turned on
The night time or any other time of the day in which visibility conditions are poor due to weather conditions.
The time period in which the vehicle’s lights must be turned on while driving in a freeway
The night time period, between sunset and sunrise
explanation: Lighting up time is legally defined as night hours or any other time when weather or similar conditions reduce visibility enough that vehicle lights are needed, not merely a fixed clock period.

question: Define “parking”
answers: Stopping a vehicle for a defined period of time, in order to unload cargo, intermittently
Stopping the vehicle for more than thirty seconds
Standing a vehicle in order to load it with cargo only, intermittently
Standing a vehicle for an uninterrupted period of time, not for the purpose of immediate loading or unloading of passengers or loading or unloading of goods.
explanation: Parking is legally defined as standing a vehicle for an uninterrupted period that is not for the immediate loading or unloading of passengers or goods, which is what separates it from a mere stop.

question: A utility tractor is a tractor type that:
answers: Has at least two wheels, an all up weight of not more than 1,500 kg, and is steered with a handlebar
Has four wheels, an unlimited all up weight, and is steered with a handlebar
Has at least three wheels and an all up weight of more than 12,000 kg
Has at least four wheels, an all up weight of not more than 1,500 kg, and is steered with a wheel
explanation: A utility tractor is defined by specific technical criteria: at least four wheels, an all-up weight capped at 1,500 kg, and steering by a wheel rather than a handlebar.

question: Define “ATV (All Terrain Vehicle)”:
answers: A vehicle that has at least four wheels, with the rider sitting astride the vehicle and steering with handlebars.
A vehicle that has at least four wheels and is steered with a wheel.
A vehicle that has at least two wheels, with the rider sitting astride the vehicle and steering with handlebars.
A vehicle that has at least four wheels and is steered with a wheel. The driver sits on it with both legs on one side of the seat.
explanation: An ATV is legally defined by having at least four wheels with the rider seated astride the vehicle and steering it using handlebars, distinguishing it from wheel-steered vehicles.

question: When a no stopping sign (433) is placed on the right side of a two-way highway:
answers: Stopping is prohibited on both sides of the vehicle.
Stopping is prohibited on the right side of the roadway and on the hard shoulder.
Stopping is prohibited on the roadway only.
Stopping is prohibited on the hard shoulder only.
explanation: No-stopping sign 433 posted on the right of a two-way road prohibits stopping on the right side of the roadway itself and on the adjoining hard shoulder, since both are part of that side of the road.

question: Define “one way street”
answers: Any path in which vehicle traffic is allowed in one direction only
Any roadway in which vehicle traffic is allowed in one direction only
Any roadway in which only motor vehicle traffic is allowed in one direction only
Any roadway in which vehicle traffic is allowed in both directions
explanation: A one-way street is legally defined as a roadway in which vehicle traffic is permitted in only one direction, tying the definition specifically to the paved roadway rather than any path.

question: What is “night time”?
answers: The period of time in which it is required to turn on the vehicle’s parking lights
A period of heavy fog only
The period of time that starts 15 minutes following sunset and ends 15 minutes before sunrise
The period of time between sunset and the following sunrise.
explanation: Night time is legally defined as the period beginning 15 minutes after sunset and ending 15 minutes before sunrise, a fixed buffer rather than the full sunset-to-sunrise span.

question: The following picture shows a pavement. Which of the following sentences is correct?
answers: Motorcycles are permitted to use the pavement instead of the road.
The pavement is designed for pedestrians only.
Private passenger vehicles are always permitted to park temporarily on the pavement, when there is no parking space on the road.
Bicyclists are permitted to ride on the pavement as well.
explanation: By law the pavement is reserved for pedestrian use; vehicles, including bicycles and motorcycles, are not permitted to use it as an alternative to the roadway.

question: What is an “Interchange”?
answers: The area that is formed by the meeting of at least three roadways, at the same level.
A meeting of at least two roadways at the same level in a freeway.
A meeting point of roads at different levels, in which it is possible to drive and pass from one road to the other
A junction of roads at the same level in an urban area.
explanation: An interchange is defined as a meeting point of roads at different levels connected in a way that allows drivers to pass from one road to the other, unlike a same-level junction.

question: “Permitted load” on a commercial vehicle is:
answers: The maximum weight of the cargo (in Kg) that is permitted to be loaded on the vehicle
The weight of the cargo plus the vehicle’s own weight
The all up weight of a transport vehicle
The vehicle’s own weight, including: water, oil, fuel and the weight of the driver
explanation: Permitted load refers strictly to the maximum weight of cargo, measured in kilograms, that a commercial vehicle is licensed to carry, separate from the vehicle's own weight.

question: The boundary of the intersection / junction is determined by:
answers: The stop lines on each of the roads that meet in the intersection
The place in which traffic signs are posted before the intersection
The imaginary line drawn between the pavements or kerbs of each road meeting the junction.
The meeting of two or more pedestrian crossings in the intersection
explanation: The boundary of a junction is fixed by the imaginary line drawn between the pavements or kerbs of the roads that meet there, giving a precise legal edge to where the junction begins.

question: A back seat passenger must wear a seatbelt. Who is held responsible if a back seat passenger doesn’t wear his seat-belt?
answers: The driver only
The driver and the passenger
The passenger only
The owner of the vehicle
explanation: Traffic law places responsibility on both the driver and the passenger for ensuring a back-seat passenger wears their seatbelt, so failing to buckle up exposes both to liability.

question: What is a “pedestrian crossing”?
answers: A part of the pavement that is marked for pedestrian crossing
A part of the road designated and marked for pedestrians to cross.
A part of the road edge that is marked for pedestrian crossing
A part of the road that is marked for pedestrian crossing, including the pavement
explanation: A pedestrian crossing is defined as a part of the road itself, not the pavement, that is designated and marked for pedestrians to cross.

question: Define level crossing:
answers: A place where a road and a railroad meet on a freeway.
A place where a road and a railroad meet at different levels.
A place where a road and a railroad meet or cross at the same level.
Any place where a railroad can be crossed
explanation: A level crossing is legally defined as a point where a road and a railroad meet or cross at the same grade, distinguishing it from crossings at different levels such as bridges.

question: What is “all up weight”?
answers: A vehicle’s own weight, as approved by the Licensing Authority
A vehicle’s own weight, plus the weight of the people and cargo that the vehicle is allowed to drive or carry, as approved by the Licensing Authority
A vehicle’s own volume plus the weight of the people and cargo it is allowed to drive or carry, as approved by the Licensing Authority
The volume of the vehicle and of the cargo it is allowed to drive or carry, as approved by the Licensing Authority
explanation: All up weight is defined as the vehicle's own weight plus the maximum weight of people and cargo it is licensed to carry, as approved by the Licensing Authority.

question: What is “own weight”?
answers: The vehicle’s weight with cargo but without the driver.
The vehicle’s weight without cargo and without the driver.
The vehicle’s weight with cargo and with a driver
The vehicle’s volume without cargo but without the driver
explanation: Own weight is the vehicle's base weight alone, excluding any cargo and excluding the driver, which is what distinguishes it from all up weight.

question: When a driver gives “right of way”, it means that:
answers: He merges with traffic without causing an accident
He allows other drivers to continue driving without causing them to change their speed or to stop
He barely manages to push into the traffic flow
He enters the traffic flow in the same speed as the other vehicles.
explanation: Giving right of way means letting other drivers continue their movement without forcing them to change speed or stop, which is the practical test for whether right of way was actually granted.

question: When is it permitted to overtake, in one go, two vehicle that are driving before you on your lane
answers: Only on highways.
When overtaking is not prohibited, and when the overtaking can be safely completed.
This type of overtaking is absolutely prohibited by law.
Only when overtaking two private passenger cars.
explanation: Overtaking two vehicles in a single maneuver is allowed whenever overtaking is not otherwise prohibited at that location and the maneuver can be completed safely, following the general rules governing all overtaking.

question: Define an “axle” of a vehicle:
answers: The vehicle’s back beam to which the vehicle’s spare wheel is connected.
A shaft which transmits the rotary motion from the gearbox to the engine.
Shaft or system of shafts running the width of the vehicle attached to the wheels.
The vehicle’s front part, designed to absorb the impact of low-speed collisions
explanation: An axle is technically defined as a shaft or system of shafts running the width of the vehicle and attached to the wheels, a structural definition distinct from engine or body parts.

question: Who is a “road user”?
answers: A person who uses the road for standing or running only
A person who uses the road for riding a motor vehicle only
A person who uses the road for bicycle riding only
A person who uses the road for driving, traveling, riding, walking, standing or any other purpose
explanation: A road user is defined broadly as anyone using the road for driving, traveling, riding, walking, standing, or any other purpose, not only those operating a vehicle.

question: Define “to dip the lights”:
answers: Turning off the high beam and turning on the fog lights
Changing the height of the parking beam
Reverting from low beam to high beam.
Reverting from high beam to low beam.
explanation: To dip the lights specifically means switching from high beam down to low beam, the standard action taken to avoid dazzling oncoming or leading drivers.

question: Define “Junction”:
answers: A meeting point of two roads or more.
The area formed by the junction of two or more roads at different levels.
The area formed by the junction of a railroad and a roadway
The junction of two urban roadways, provided that they are both asphalt-paved.
explanation: A junction is defined simply as the meeting point of two or more roads, without requiring a specific surface type or urban setting.

question: Define “stop line”:
answers: A line drawn on either full or half width across the road marking a stopping point for vehicles.
A line along the road, marking the point in which a vehicle must stop, in junctions with traffic lights only.
A line along the road, marking the point in which a vehicle must stop, before a railway crossing
A junction-line along the road, either full or partial, marking the point in which a vehicle must stop near a pavement
explanation: A stop line is defined generally as a line, full or partial width, marking a stopping point for vehicles, which applies wherever a stop is legally required and not only at signal-controlled junctions.

question: Define “play street”:
answers: A main road joined by side roads.
A road designed for children’s games, pedestrians and vehicles, sign posted at the entrance with the “play street” sign.
A street designated for children’s games, into which only pedestrians and two wheeled vehicles are permitted to enter.
A street in which different types of vehicles may drive side by side
explanation: A play street is legally defined as a road designed for children's games as well as pedestrian and vehicle use, identified by the specific play-street sign posted at its entrance.

question: What is a “rigid veicle”?
answers: A vehicle body which exceeds the size of a normal vehicle.
A vehicle body in which the driver’s compartment is separated from the trunk.
A vehicle body with a partition between the driver’s seat and the passengers.
A vehicle body in which the driver’s compartment and the trunk comprise one unit.
explanation: A rigid vehicle body is one in which the driver's compartment and the cargo trunk form a single continuous unit, distinguishing it from articulated or separated-body vehicles.

question: Define “slow moving vehicle”:
answers: A motor vehicle having a prescribed maximal speed of 50 k.p.h.
A motor vehicle having a prescribed maximal speed of no less than 50 k.p.h.
A vehicle restricted by law to 40 k.p.h. or less
A motor vehicle having a prescribed maximal speed of 55 k.p.h.
explanation: A slow-moving vehicle is legally defined by having a maximum permitted speed capped at 40 km/h or less, which is why lower speed limits and overtaking caution apply around such vehicles.

question: Which of the following is an emergency vehicle?
answers: A Red Magen David Ambulance, an Israel Police vehicle, IDF vehicle, Fire-fighting vehicle, integrated policing vehicle or any other vehicle approved by the Authority, when it sounds its emergency signals and operates flashing lights and sounds an alarm signal.
Any ambulance, IDF vehicle, fire-fighting vehicle or other commercial vehicle that was authorized to function as an emergency vehicle by the Licensing Authority
Every vehicle of the Israel Police or the IDF and vehicles that are used for regular security missions in borderline settlements
A vehicle of the Israel Police or the IDF and a fire-fighting vehicle only
explanation: A vehicle only counts legally as an emergency vehicle when it is an authorized type, such as an ambulance, police, IDF, or fire vehicle, and is actively sounding its alarm and operating its flashing emergency lights.

question: Is it permitted to drive passengers for hire in a private passenger car?
answers: Yes, if a contract is signed between the driver and the passengers
Yes, if the vehicle is equipped with a standard chassis, approved by the Licensing Authority
No
No, except with a permission of the Tax Authorities
explanation: Carrying passengers for hire in a private passenger car is simply not permitted, since fare-paying transport requires a vehicle licensed for public or commercial use, and no private contract can substitute for that license.

question: What is the definition of an “obsolete vehicle” in regard to private passenger cars?
answers: A private passenger car is not included in the definition of an “obsolete vehicle”.
A private passenger car that was manufactured more than 19 years ago.
A private passenger car that was manufactured more than 15 years ago.
A vehicle that does not meet the compelling Israeli standard.
explanation: For a private passenger car, the law defines an obsolete vehicle as one manufactured more than 19 years ago, a fixed age threshold rather than a condition-based test.

question: What is a “private passenger car”?
answers: A public motor vehicle, designed to carry eight passengers, licensed as a public vehicle
A private motor vehicle, designed to carry up to eight passengers, apart from the driver and stated on the vehicle license private vehicle.
A motor vehicle, designed to carry ten passengers, licensed as a private vehicle
A private motor vehicle, designed to carry at least twelve passengers, licensed as a private vehicle
explanation: A private passenger car is legally defined as a private motor vehicle designed to carry up to eight passengers besides the driver and registered on its license as a private vehicle.

question: When a vehicle is disqualified from use on the road:
answers: It is forbidden to be on the road without authorization from the licensing authority.
It is forbidden to get back on the road without authorization of the insurance company
It is allowed to stay on the road for a period of up to seven days after being taken off the road.
It is allowed to stay on the road unlimitedly, as long as it doesn’t pose any traffic safety risk
explanation: Once a vehicle is disqualified from use, it is forbidden to be on the road again without authorization from the Licensing Authority, since the disqualification remains in force until officially lifted.

question: Define “path”:
answers: Part of the width of the road designated for pedestrians only.
A part of the road, designed for motorcycle traffic only.
Lane or part of a lane that is not a road and designated for specific users.
A part of the road, which was marked by the “Israel’s Paths” Company.
explanation: A path is legally distinguished from a road by being a lane or part of a lane that is not itself a road and is designated for specific users, such as pedestrians or cyclists.

question: When driving in reverse:
answers: You must use another person to guide you.
You must use another person to guide you on highways..
You must use another person to guide you during "lighting up time".
You are permitted to use another person to guide you.
explanation: The law makes using another person as a guide while reversing a permitted practice rather than an absolute requirement, leaving the decision to the driver based on the situation's difficulty.

question: After parking your car besides the pavement, on the right side of an urban road:
answers: You should verify that the passenger sitting in the left back seat gets out very carefully from the car to the road.
You should verify that the maximal distance between the car and the pavement is one meter.
Before getting out of the car, you should verify that this will not disturb any road user.
If the street is not lit, you should turn on the parking lights.
explanation: Before getting out of a parked car, the driver has a duty of care to verify that opening the door and exiting will not disturb or endanger any other road user.

question: Define “built dividing area”:
answers: A separation area which divides the road lengthwise by means of an elevated structure above the road way
The area along a roadway, in which road users can stop, park their vehicles or stand in for refreshment
Any area that is marked on the road on which it is forbidden to drive
Any part of the road (pavement, hard shoulder, traffic island) which is elevated above the road way.
explanation: A built dividing area is defined as a separation area that divides the road lengthwise by means of an elevated physical structure, distinguishing it from a merely painted or marked division.

question: What is a “safety seat”:
answers: A seat meeting specified standards installed on two-wheelers and designed for transporting children.
A seat, meeting specified standards, secured to the vehicle with a safety belt and used for transporting children with independent belts.
Any seat that is adjusted for driving children and elderly people and meets the standard which was set by the Ministry of Environmental Protection
A seat which is installed inside a vehicle during its manufacture-stage and is adjusted for driving children with a maximum age of 14 years
explanation: A safety seat must meet a defined standard, be secured to the vehicle using a seatbelt, and restrain the child with the seat's own independent harness, which is what separates it from a simple booster.

question: What is a “booster seat”?
answers: A seat that is designed for transporting small children, restrained by the safety belt of the vehicle.
A standard seat that is designed for transporting children until 18 years of age
A seat that is designed for a driver whose height is less than 160 cm and whose age is more than 18 years
A seat that is designed for transporting children on bicycles only while the children are restrained by a safety belt.
explanation: A booster seat is designed to raise a small child so that the vehicle's own seatbelt can properly restrain them, rather than providing its own separate harness.

question: Define “motor vehicle”:
answers: A vehicle propelled by a diesel engine only
A vehicle propelled by a gasoline engine only.
A vehicle, propelled by any power or mechanical means.
A vehicle with at least two wheels.
explanation: A motor vehicle is legally defined broadly as any vehicle propelled by any power or mechanical means, not limited to a particular fuel or engine type.

question: Which documents should a driver be in possession of whilst driving?
answers: Valid driving license, vehicle registration, compulsory insurance certificate and any other lawfully issued certificate
Driving license and vehicle registration only
Identity card, driving license, comprehensive insurance certificate and a certification of a towing arrangement for the vehicle
Identity card, driving license and a certificate testifying about the vehicle’s proper functioning signed by a manager of a garage
explanation: The law requires a driver to carry a valid driving license, the vehicle's registration, a compulsory insurance certificate, and any other document lawfully required to be held while driving.

question: When may a driver be in possession of only photocopies of his original vehicle documents?
answers: Only a vehicle transport company is allowed to hold a photocopy of the vehicle registration
It is only permitted when the vehicle is owned by a corporation, and the photocopied documents’ validity is authorized by the safety officer’s signature and stamp on them.
When the vehicle is owned by a private person, and the photocopy is certified by the vehicle owner’s signature
Never. The driver must always be in possession of the original documents
explanation: Photocopies of vehicle documents may substitute for originals only when the vehicle belongs to a corporation and the copies bear the authorizing signature and stamp of the safety officer.

question: Is a driver obliged to show a policeman the vehicle’s original documents?
answers: Yes, at a time and place to be determined by the policeman
No, a certified photocopy is sufficient
No, a photocopy signed by the vehicle’s owner is sufficient
Yes, at the time determined by the vehicle’s driver
explanation: A driver must produce the vehicle's original documents to a policeman at whatever time and place the officer determines, since a photocopy alone does not satisfy this legal duty.

question: The lawful “point system for traffic offenses” is:
answers: A system for issuing demerit points to drivers who are convicted of committing traffic offences once every five years.
A system for issuing demerit points to drivers who were convicted of committing offences against the traffic regulations.
A system through which courts are notified about vehicle improper functioning.
A system for registering convictions in criminal offences.
explanation: The points system exists to record demerit points against drivers convicted of traffic-regulation offenses, allowing repeat offenders to be identified and addressed.

question: In what condition should the driver and vehicle’s document be kept?
answers: The law doesn’t provide any explicit reference to this issue
It is enough if they are stainless and have a clear photo.
They should be kept at home, clean and readable at all times.
They should always be kept inside the car, clean and readable
explanation: The law requires that the driver's and the vehicle's documents always be kept inside the car, clean and readable, so they can be produced properly whenever needed.

question: Where should a “new driver” sign be placed?
answers: At the center of the vehicle rear window’s top edge, visible to other drivers from all sides
On the top edge of the vehicle’s left side window, visible to those driving on the left of the vehicle
On the bottom edge of the vehicle’s rear window, visible to those driving behind
On the bottom edge of the vehicle’s right side window, visible to those driving on the right of the vehicle
explanation: The new-driver sign must be placed on the bottom edge of the vehicle's rear window so it is clearly visible to traffic driving behind the vehicle.

question: For how long should a driver place a “new driver” sign on his rear window?
answers: For a period of two years or for as long as he is a new driver
For a period of nine months
For a period of six months
For a period of three months
explanation: A new driver must display the sign for two years, or for as long as new-driver status applies, whichever period is relevant to that individual driver.

question: Is it permitted to make changes in the vehicle or driver’s documentation?
answers: It is permitted only to highlight writings that were erased or made unclear over time
It is permitted only to add or change an address, in the main post office branch
It is permitted only to add the zip code of a residence address, in the main post office branch
No. Only the Licensing Authority is allowed to change details in these documents.
explanation: Only the Licensing Authority is legally empowered to make changes to the details recorded in a vehicle's or driver's official documents; no self-made alterations are permitted.

question: Which changes in health condition must be reported to the Licensing Authority?
answers: The driver doesn’t have to report anything to the Licensing Authority, but only to the Ministry of Health
Any detection of the following conditions: heart disease or any limitation of the nervous system, bones, eye-sight and hearing
The driver doesn’t have to report anything to the Licensing Authority. The report shall be made by the treating physician of the driver
A driver doesn’t have to report about changes in his health, except in case of a neurological problem
explanation: A driver must report specific health changes to the Licensing Authority, including detection of heart disease or limitations affecting the nervous system, bones, eyesight, or hearing, since these directly affect fitness to drive.

question: Should every road user obey the traffic signs?
answers: Yes, while on the sidewalk only.
Yes, every road user should obey the road signs.
No, only vehicle drivers should obey the traffic signs
Yes, while on the road way only.
explanation: Traffic signs bind every road user, not only vehicle drivers, since signs regulate the conduct of all people using the road, including pedestrians.

question: Do traffic light instructions have priority over “right-of-way giving” signs?
answers: No, In legal terms, the instructions of a traffic light and the instructions of traffic signs are of equal effect
No, but a stop sign has priority over a green light for traffic moving in the same direction
Yes, traffic light instructions have priority over any type of traffic sign, except for a flashing yellow light
Sometimes. Traffic light instructions have priority in an urban way only
explanation: Traffic light signals take priority over right-of-way giving signs, with the single exception of a flashing yellow light, in which case the applicable priority sign governs instead.

question: Is it obligatory to obey the directions and signals of a policeman in uniform?
answers: Yes, always, while taking extra precautions
No, only to the directions of a traffic policeman
No, only if the policeman is on duty
Yes, only as regards to traffic directions
explanation: The directions and signals of a uniformed policeman must always be obeyed, though drivers should exercise extra caution when following them.

question: Is it obligatory to obey the directions of a policeman who has identified himself with an appropriate certificate?
answers: No. you must only obey a traffic policeman who directs traffic in an intersection.
Yes, even if his directions contradict those of a road sign.
Generally not.
Yes, but only concerning traffic directions that are given within the intersection.
explanation: Once a policeman has properly identified themselves, their directions must be obeyed even when they contradict a posted road sign, since a live traffic direction overrides the static sign.

question: Is it obligatory to obey the directions and signals of a municipal inspector in uniform?
answers: No. It is only obligatory to obey as regards to parking directions within city limits
No. It is only obligatory to obey as regards to the presentation of a driver’s license
Usually not
Yes, if the directions are related to traffic control.
explanation: A uniformed municipal inspector's directions are binding specifically when those directions relate to traffic control, giving inspectors limited but real authority over road users.

question: Is it obligatory to obey the directions of a Public Works Department employee in uniform?
answers: No, unless he directs you to stop on the road’s “hard shoulders” only.
Yes, but on urban roads only.
Yes, wherever road pavement or maintenance works are conducted.
No, it is only obligatory to obey a policeman in uniform,
explanation: A uniformed Public Works Department employee's directions must be obeyed wherever road pavement or maintenance works are being conducted, since they are managing safety around the worksite.

question: Is it obligatory to obey the directions and signals of a military policeman in uniform?
answers: No, only for the purpose of stopping a vehicle
Yes, equally to a civil policeman
No, only as regards to the presentation of a driver’s license
Usually not
explanation: A uniformed military policeman's directions and signals carry the same binding legal force as those of a civilian police officer.

question: Is it permitted to overtake, or to try overtaking, another vehicle within a distance of 100 meters before a railway crossing?
answers: Yes, if the overtaken vehicle is a motorcycle .
Yes, provided that a train is neither seen nor heard.
Yes, if the overtaken vehicle is a tractor.
It is absolutely forbidden.
explanation: Overtaking is completely forbidden within 100 meters of a railway crossing regardless of the vehicle type being passed or whether a train is currently visible, since the added risk near a crossing makes any attempt too dangerous.

question: When you approach a pedestrian crossing:
answers: You are allowed to overtake in a one way road.
Do not overtake and do not try to overtake any other vehicle before the crossing.
You are allowed to overtake if there are no pedestrians on the crossing.
You are allowed to overtake before the pedestrian crossing in an urban road only.
explanation: Drivers must not overtake, or even attempt to overtake, as they approach a pedestrian crossing, because doing so could hide a crossing pedestrian from view or force a vehicle onto the crossing at an unsafe moment.

question: When crossing an intersection with one lane in each driving direction:
answers: You are allowed to overtake, but you must finish the overtaking after the intersection.
You are allowed to overtake carefully vehicles with more than two wheels.
You are only allowed to overtake a slow vehicle.
It is prohibited to overtake and it is prohibited to try to overtake within the intersection’s boundaries, except if you are overtaking a two-wheeler.
explanation: Overtaking is prohibited within an intersection's boundaries because of the added risk from crossing traffic, with a narrow exception for passing a two-wheeled vehicle, which poses far less risk of a serious collision.

question: When are you forbidden to overtake another vehicle?
answers: In a two-way interurban road.
When driving in a left-turn lane.
When the vehicle on your right drives slow.
When the other vehicle stops before an intersection or before a pedestrian crossing or before a railway crossing.
explanation: A driver may not overtake a vehicle that has stopped before an intersection, a pedestrian crossing, or a railway crossing, since that vehicle may be yielding to a hazard, such as cross traffic or a train, that is not yet visible to the overtaking driver.

question: What should a driver of an overtaken vehicle do?
answers: He should continue driving without changing his speed and driving lane.
An overtaken vehicle should take no interest in the overtaking vehicle, and should continue driving normally.
Deviate as much as possible to the road’s edge, without changing his speed.
Stop at the side of the road and allow the traffic to pass him.
explanation: The vehicle being overtaken should move as far toward the edge of the road as it safely can while keeping its speed steady, making room for the overtaking vehicle without creating unpredictable braking or acceleration.

question: When is a driver required to drive on an asphalt paved hard shoulder?
answers: When driving a commercial motor vehicle with an overall permissible weight of more than 10,000 Kg.
When driving a motor vehicle that is forced to drive at a slow speed due to the cargo it is carrying or to the slope of the road.
When driving a bus with an overall permissible weight of more than 10,000 Kg.
Never. The law prohibits driving on the road’s edges.
explanation: A driver forced to travel slowly because of a heavy load or a steep gradient must use the paved hard shoulder where one is available, so as not to obstruct normal-speed traffic in the regular lanes.

question: What gap should be maintained from the vehicle that is driving in front of us?
answers: A gap of thirty meters, in order to allow safe stoppage.
A gap of forty meters, in order to prevent an accident.
A gap of at least three seconds.
A gap which always allows us to stop and prevent a collision..
explanation: Traffic law requires keeping whatever gap from the vehicle ahead is needed to stop in time and avoid a collision under the current speed and road conditions, rather than relying on a single fixed distance that fits every situation.

question: What is the minimal gap that you should legally maintain from the vehicle in front of you?
answers: The distance traveled in at least three second of driving (the 21…22…23 count system)
At least twenty two meters.
The distance traveled in two seconds of driving.
The distance traveled in one second of driving.
explanation: The legal floor for the following gap is the distance covered in one second of travel, since anything closer leaves no real separation, even though safer practice, based on reaction-time studies, recommends a larger two-to-three second gap.

question: What  is a reasonable vehicle speed?
answers: On paved roads – 80KpH; on dirt roads – 40KpH.
The maximum speed the vehicle can reach under the existing circumstances.
A reasonable speed which, considering all the road conditions, and road signs allows the driver to control the vehicle
Any speed, as long as the driver fully controls the vehicle.
explanation: Reasonable speed is defined by law as a speed that lets the driver keep full control of the vehicle given the actual road, traffic, and weather conditions and any posted signs, not a fixed number or the vehicle's mechanical top speed.

question: Under which circumstances should you slow down your driving?
answers: When your vehicle or any passerby and property are at risk.
When passing under a bridge.
In a two-way roadway having 4 lanes.
When entering an acceleration lane.
explanation: A driver must slow down whenever continuing at the current speed would put their own vehicle, another road user, or property at risk, since this general duty of care overrides any specific posted speed limit.

question: In which cases are you legally obliged to slow down?
answers: When the road is obstructed, or having poor visibility or sharp bends.
Before and during overtaking, for increased safety.
In a place that is shaded by a boulevard of high trees.
When you approach a place in which delinquent activity might take place.
explanation: The law requires slowing down whenever the road is obstructed, visibility is poor, or the road has sharp bends, since these conditions reduce a driver's ability to see hazards and to stop or steer away from them in time.

question: When you arrive with your vehicle to the place that is illustrated in the following picture, you must:
answers: Slow down.
Honk.
Accelerate.
Stop.
explanation: The scenario shown calls for reducing speed rather than a full stop, a honk, or acceleration, because the depicted hazard or caution point requires the driver to retain full control while approaching it, not necessarily to halt outright.

question: In which cases are you obliged to slow down?
answers: You are only obliged to slow down in case of busy traffic.
When encountering or overtaking an animal.
There is no obligation to slow down. There is an obligation to drive carefully.
You are obliged to slow down in an urban road only.
explanation: Drivers must slow down around an animal on or near the road, since a sudden loud engine or a close pass can startle the animal into an unpredictable movement directly into the vehicle's path.

question: According to the following picture you are obliged to:
answers: Stop.
Slow down.
Accelerate.
Honk.
explanation: The picture indicates a hazard or caution situation calling for reduced speed so the driver retains full control and reaction time, rather than stopping outright, honking, or accelerating.

question: When is it permitted to perform an emergency stop?
answers: After signaling a distress sign to the vehicle behind you only.
In order to prevent a road accident that cannot be prevented in any other way.
When the driving speed doesn’t fit with the road conditions.
When the road is distorted.
explanation: An emergency stop is justified only as a last resort to prevent a road accident that cannot be avoided in any other way, since braking hard without real cause creates its own collision risk for following traffic.

question: Is it permitted to perform an emergency brake for any reason other than to prevent a road accident?
answers: Yes, in a dirt road only, at a distance of 200 meters from buildings.
Yes, after signaling a distress sign to the vehicle behind you.
Yes, for brake-testing, provided that it does not disturb or endanger any other road user.
Yes, in a paved road only, at a distance of 200 meters from buildings.
explanation: Emergency braking for a reason other than avoiding an accident is allowed only for testing the brakes, and only when it causes no danger or disturbance to any other road user, making it a narrow, conditional exception.

question: Which vehicles are permitted to enter a freeway?
answers: Only private motor vehicles.
Every motor and non-motor vehicle.
A motor vehicle which is permitted and capable of driving at the speed that is indicated on the road sign.
Every motor vehicle, except for heavy trucks which might disturb traffic due to their low speed.
explanation: Only a motor vehicle that is both permitted and mechanically capable of maintaining the speed shown on the freeway's sign may enter, since a slower vehicle would create a serious hazard mixing with the freeway's high-speed traffic.

question: What is the maximum permitted speed for driving an all-terrain vehicle?
answers: 30 KPH.
50 KPH in any type of road.
60 KPH in a freeway and 40 KPH in any other type of road.
40 KPH in any type of road.
explanation: An all-terrain vehicle's maximum permitted speed is capped at 40 km/h on every type of road, including freeways, reflecting this vehicle category's lower design speed and stability limits.

question: When is it lawfully required to perform a vehicle license test?
answers: Every two years, for all vehicle types.
Every two years for commercial vehicles and every year for motorcycles.
Every two years for all types of private passenger vehicles, without any restriction on the vehicle’s age.
Every year or any other lawfully defined period.
explanation: The legally required interval for a vehicle roadworthiness test varies by vehicle type and age, as set by law, rather than following a single uniform two-year rule that applies to every vehicle without distinction.

question: What is the maximum permitted speed for driving a private passenger vehicle on a freeway(motorway) (unless otherwise indicted)
answers: 110 KPH.
90 KPH.
80 KPH.
100 KPH.
explanation: For a private passenger car, the default maximum speed on a freeway, unless a sign states otherwise, is 110 km/h, as set out in the maximum permitted speed regulations for this road category.

question: What is the maximum speed for a private passenger vehicle, driven on an inter–urban road with a central divider (if not indicated otherwise by a traffic sign)?
answers: 90 KPH.
110 KPH.
100 KPH.
80 KPH.
explanation: An inter-urban road with a constructed central median divider carries a default maximum speed of 90 km/h for a private passenger vehicle, higher than an undivided inter-urban road because the physical divider removes the risk of head-on conflict.

question: What is the maximum permitted speed for driving a private passenger vehicle (if not indicated otherwise by a traffic sign)?
answers: In an urban road – up to 50 KPH and in a freeway – up to 70 KPH
In an urban area – up to 50 KPH and on an inter-urban road – up to 80 KPH
In an urban road – according to road conditions, and in a freeway – up to 100 KPH
In an urban road – up to 40 KPH and in a freeway – up to 80 KPH
explanation: Unless signs state otherwise, a private passenger vehicle's default maximum speed is 50 km/h in an urban area and 80 km/h on an ordinary inter-urban road, reflecting the higher pedestrian and junction density found in town.

question: What is the meaning of the traffic sign in the following picture?
answers: It is a speed restriction that is intended for private vehicles only.
The vehicle’s driving speed should not be lesser than 40 KPH.
It is a speed restriction that is intended for two-wheelers and trolleys.
The vehicle’s driving speed should not exceed 40 KPH.
explanation: A regulatory speed sign of this type sets a maximum, meaning the vehicle's driving speed must not exceed the number shown; it establishes an upper limit rather than a minimum, and applies generally rather than to a single vehicle category.

question: What is the maximum allowed speed in a “play street”?
answers: 10 KPH.
20 KPH.
40 KPH.
30 KPH.
explanation: A 'play street,' where children and pedestrians are expected to be present, carries a legal maximum speed of 30 km/h, lower than an ordinary residential street, so that any unavoidable close encounter remains survivable.

question: What must a driver do when approaching a railway crossing?
answers: Continue driving normally. You don’t have to slow down.
Stop, open the vehicle’s windows and listen
Stop at a distance of at least one meter before the railway.
Slow down to a speed which will allow him to stop before the crossing.if necessary.
explanation: Approaching a railway crossing, a driver must reduce speed enough that the vehicle can be stopped before the tracks if that turns out to be necessary, rather than driving through at normal speed or requiring a full stop in every case.

question: What must a driver do when approaching a railway crossing barrier which is marked by a traffic light?
answers: Turn off the vehicle’s radio only.
Act normally. The driver must drive carefully only when he sees or hears an approaching train.
Act normally. When a railway crossing is protected by a barrier, the driver is allowed to be less alert.
He must always slow down.
explanation: A driver must always slow down when approaching a railway barrier controlled by a traffic light, regardless of whether a train is currently visible or audible, since the crossing remains a heightened-risk area at all times.

question: Where should you stop your vehicle when you are obliged to stop before a railway crossing?
answers: In the place with the best field of view, without disturbing train traffic.
After the stop line, eight meters before the proximate rail.
Before the stop line. If there is no stop line – before the barrier.. If there is no barrier – at least four meters before the nearest rail.
Before the barrier. If there is no barrier – six meters before the nearest rail.
explanation: The law sets a specific fallback order for where to stop at a railway crossing: at the stop line if marked, otherwise before the barrier, and if there is no barrier, at least four meters before the nearest rail, keeping the vehicle clear of danger in every configuration.

question: When you approach a railway crossing and an approaching train is seen, heard or sounds a warning signal:
answers: You should stop before the railway crossing until the train passes.
If the train is far, you should quickly cross the rails.
You should accelerate and cross the rails before the train arrives, in a careful and watchful manner.
You should carefully cross the rails, in any fitting speed.
explanation: Once a train is seen, heard, or signaled by a warning device, the driver must stop before the crossing and wait until it has fully passed; attempting to cross ahead of the train, at any speed, is never permitted.

question: How should you conduct yourself when a “stop” sign is placed before a railway crossing?
answers: You must stop when an approaching train is seen or heard.
You have to stop during the night. There is no obligation to stop during the day.
Stop the vehicle, turn off the radio, television or tape set, and open the window next to you.
Stop, as in any other place in which a “stop” sign is placed, and then continue driving.
explanation: When a stop sign is posted before a railway crossing, the driver must make a full, deliberate stop, turn off any radio or media playing, and open the window to listen for an approaching train, not just perform the usual brief stop-and-go.

question: Is it permitted to drive through a railway crossing when the barrier is moving downwards or upwards?
answers: It is permitted to drive through, as long as you drive carefully.
It is allowed for as long as the barrier doesn’t reach its bottom position and locks.
It is allowed when the barrier starts to rise.
No.It is prohibited for as long as the barrier is in movement to any direction or when it is horizontally positioned.
explanation: Driving through a railway crossing is prohibited for as long as the barrier is moving in either direction or lying horizontal, since a moving or lowered barrier signals that a train is approaching or still clearing the crossing.

question: When are you obliged to stop before a railway crossing?
answers: When a “railway crossing” sign is placed.
When a “right of way for crossing traffic” sign is placed.
You don’t have to stop. Stop at your own discretion when a train is seen and is approaching.
When the train is seen, heard or sounds a warning signal.
explanation: The duty to stop before a railway crossing is triggered by an approaching train actually being seen, heard, or announced by a warning signal, not solely by the presence of a particular static sign at that location.

question: What should you do when approaching a railway crossing and a warning signal is given before you reached the crossing:
answers: Stop and don’t continue driving.
Slow down only when a signaler turns on a warning signal.
Slow down only if you see an approaching train.
Ignore the signal and continue driving. You were there before the signal.
explanation: If a warning signal activates before a driver reaches the crossing, they must stop and not proceed, since the signal itself creates the stopping obligation regardless of whether an oncoming train can personally be seen.

question: When are you required to turn on the direction indicators and signal?
answers: When you approach a railway crossing or a pedestrian crossing.
Only before a sharp curve.
Only when you make left hand turns in intersections.
When you are about to start driving or to turn your vehicle, or to deviate from your lane.
explanation: Direction indicators must be used whenever a driver is about to pull away, turn, or move out of their lane, since this signaling duty is general and continuous, not limited to specific locations such as crossings or particular turn types.

question: Is it obligatory to signal while deviating to the right or to the left from the driving lane?
answers: It is not obligatory to signal while deviating from one lane to the other.
It is not obligatory to signal during an insignificant deviation from the lane.
It is obligatory to signal before any deviation from the driving lane, until it is completed.
It is not obligatory to signal if the deviation is significant and noticed by all drivers
explanation: Signaling is mandatory before beginning any deviation from the driving lane and must continue until the maneuver is complete, regardless of how small or seemingly insignificant the lane shift is.

question: When and where are you required to turn on the direction indicator?
answers: You should signal with the winker when you are 150 meters before the turn.
You should only signal before making right-hand and left-hand turns.
You should only signal when other passersby are near.
In such place and time that other road users can notice the given signal.
explanation: The rule requires giving the turn signal at whatever time and place will let other road users actually notice and react to it, rather than following a fixed distance figure that might not fit every situation.

question: How do you give a signal for braking?
answers: By turning on the four direction indicators.
By putting out the right hand through the left window.
By the brake lights.
By putting out the right hand through the right window.
explanation: A braking signal is given automatically through the vehicle's brake lights when the pedal is pressed, and is not something communicated through hand signals or the direction indicators.

question: Is it permitted to use any other means for signaling when the electric signaling system is not functioning?
answers: It is required to give signal by hand, but only in good weather conditions.
It is required under these circumstances to give signal by hand.
No. You must use the direction indicator for signaling.
It is required to give signal by hand, but only at night.
explanation: If the vehicle's electric turn signals stop working, the driver is required to give hand signals instead, regardless of weather conditions or time of day, so other road users still receive adequate warning of the intended maneuver.

question: What should you do when the electric signaling system is out of order?
answers: Signal with your left hand, as stated by law.
You may continue driving until the closest garage without giving signals - even where signaling is obligatory.
You may continue driving during “light time”. At any other time you may not.
Stop driving.
explanation: When the electric signaling system malfunctions, the law requires the driver to signal with an outstretched left hand as a substitute, rather than skipping signals or continuing to drive without them until reaching a garage.

question: What should we do when driving behind a vehicle that is giving a direction indicator signal?
answers: Stay close to the right of the road.
Continue driving without slowing down. It has nothing to do with you.
Continue driving at an accelerated speed, to minimize the conflict period.
We should allow the driver of the vehicle in front to perform the action he signaled for, by slowing down and stop if required.
explanation: Seeing a direction indicator on the vehicle ahead, a following driver should slow down, and stop if necessary, to let that vehicle safely complete the turn or lane change it has signaled for, rather than pressing on regardless.

question: When you use the vehicle’s horn for signaling:
answers: The signal shall be given at a fast and unchanging pace.
You are lawfully required to honk at least three times.
The signal should not be longer than needed.
The signal shall be given in a long and continuous manner.
explanation: When using the horn to signal, the sound should last no longer than needed to achieve its warning purpose, since prolonged or repeated honking causes unnecessary disturbance without adding any safety value.

question: When is it permitted to use the horn for giving a warning signal in an urban road?
answers: It is only allowed to use an air horn.
It is always allowed to use the horn, provided that the signal is given in a continuous and uniform manner.
It is only allowed to use the horn in order to avoid imminent danger that cannot be prevented in any other way.
It is always allowed to use the horn in an urban road.
explanation: In an urban area the horn may be used only to prevent an imminent danger that cannot be avoided any other way; it is not for general or continuous use, and using it routinely in town is not permitted.

question: The following illustration shows a wide road. Which number in it marks a road?
explanation: In this illustration a 'road' refers to the entire right-of-way used by traffic between two points, including its lanes, shoulders, and dividers together, rather than any single lane or divider marked separately within it.

question: How should you conduct yourself at an exit from a premises or from an access road to a house, when you are about to cross the sidewalk (pavement)?
answers: Stop always and give right-of-way to the vehicles that are come from the left and approaching the exit.
Slow down and even stop if required, in order to allow pedestrians to cross safely.
Stop always and give right-of-way to the pedestrians that are crossing the road.
The rule “first to come, first to go” applies to an exit from a premises or from an access road to a house. The pedestrians will wait.
explanation: When crossing a sidewalk while exiting a driveway or private property, the driver must slow down, and stop if necessary, to let pedestrians using the sidewalk pass safely, since they have priority over a vehicle emerging from a non-road exit.

question: How should you conduct yourself at an exit from a premises or from an access road to a house, when you are about to enter or cross the road?
answers: Give way to the vehicles that are driving away from you in the road you are about to enter.
The rules for giving “right-of-way” in such an exit are identical to those that apply in the case of an intersection.
You must give way to vehicles coming from the right only.
Give-way to the approaching vehicles in the road you are about to enter.
explanation: Once past the sidewalk and about to enter or cross the road itself from a private exit, the driver must give way to vehicles already approaching on that road, since a vehicle emerging from a driveway never has right of way over through traffic.

question: To which of the following should you give right-of-way when making a left turn in an intersection where no road sign is placed?
answers: To a vehicle coming from the left only.
To a vehicle coming from in front of you only.
To the fastest vehicle.
To a vehicle coming from the front and from the right.
explanation: At an intersection with no priority signs, a driver turning left must give way to vehicles coming straight through from the opposite direction and to vehicles approaching from the right, since a left turn crosses both of their paths.

question: Which of the roads in the following illustration is a one-way road?
answers: Street A and street C.
Street B and street C.
Only street C.
Street A.
explanation: A one-way road is identified in the illustration by its directional arrows or signage that permits travel in a single direction only, distinguishing it from the two-way streets shown elsewhere in the picture.

question: How should you behave when leaving a private yard a petrol station or an entrance to a properity or a house ?
answers: The rule “first to come, first to go” should be exercised at an exit from a premises or from a gas station. The pedestrians will wait.
Slow down and even stop if required, in order to allow the pedestrians to cross safely.
Stop and give right-of-way to the pedestrians that are crossing the intersection.
Stop and give right-of-way to the vehicles that are coming from the left and approaching the exit.
explanation: Leaving a private yard, a petrol station, or a property entrance, the driver must slow down and stop if needed to let pedestrians cross safely, applying the same sidewalk-priority rule as any other driveway exit.

question: How should you conduct yourself when exiting premises, a gas station or an access road to a house?
answers: You should give right-of-way to vehicles coming from the left only.
The “right-of-way” rules in such an exit are identical to those that apply to an intersection.
You should give right-of-way to vehicles coming from the right only.
Give right of way to any vehicles approaching the road you are entering and pedestrians on the pavement.
explanation: Exiting premises, a gas station, or a house's access road, the driver must give way both to vehicles already on the road being entered and to any pedestrians on the pavement being crossed, since the duty covers both groups, not just one.

question: How would you conduct yourself when approaching the intersection that is depicted in the following picture?
answers: Stop anyway.
Always accelerate when entering the intersection, in order to avoid traffic disturbance.
Cross it safely.
Slow down and even stop if necessary in order to give right-of-way.
explanation: Approaching this intersection, the driver must slow down, and stop if required, to give way as the situation demands, rather than assuming the right of way or accelerating through regardless of other traffic.

question: How should you behave when approaching the sign in the picture?
answers: Cross the place quickly and merge with traffic.
Stop and give right-of-way.
Give right-of-way to the traffic on the roadway that is to your left.
Slow down and give right-of-way to vehicles coming from your right.
explanation: This sign instructs the driver to give right of way specifically to traffic on the roadway to their left, marking that direction as having priority at this particular junction configuration.

question: How would you conduct yourself when approaching an intersection that is preceded by a “stop” sign?
answers: Stop and give right-of-way to any other vehicle that is entering or approaching the intersection from a different roadway.
Give right-of-way to any other vehicle that is entering or approaching the intersection from a different roadway.
You are only obliged to stop when vehicle traffic on the crossing road is approaching from your right.
You are only obliged to stop when a policeman instructs you to do so.
explanation: A stop sign requires the driver to stop and then give way to every other vehicle entering or approaching the intersection from any other roadway, not merely to traffic from one particular direction or only when a police officer directs it.

question: Where should you stop according to the following picture:
answers: Before and close to the stop line.
You can stop anywhere, as long as you stop before entering the intersection.
Before the signpost.
After the pedestrian crossing, but before the intersection.
explanation: When a stop sign and stop line are present, the driver must stop right before and close to that line, since the line marks the exact legal stopping point rather than leaving the driver free to stop anywhere short of the junction.

question: Where would you stop according to the following picture:
answers: At least 10 meters before the junction.
Before the signpost.
Where you can see the traffic crossing your path.
In any case – before the pedestrian crossing.
explanation: Without a marked stop line, the correct stopping point is wherever the driver gains a clear view of the traffic crossing their path, since the purpose of stopping is to actually be able to check for oncoming vehicles before proceeding.

question: What is instructed by the following road sign?
answers: Give right-of-way. There is no need to stop.
Slow down and give right-of-way.
Stop for a moment, check the traffic and continue driving.
Stop and give right-of-way.
explanation: This sign requires a full stop followed by giving way to other traffic, unlike a simple yield sign that only requires giving way without necessarily requiring the vehicle to come to a complete stop first.

question: How would you conduct yourself under the situation that is depicted in the following picture?
answers: You should not obey the traffic light signals. Follow the road signs only.
Stop before the junction and do not enter into it.
Stop before the junction and then drive through uninterruptedly.
Give right-of-way to the traffic on the crossing road.
explanation: In this situation the driver must stop before the junction and not enter it at all, since proceeding into the intersection, even partway, would leave the vehicle blocking crossing traffic or trapped without a clear path through.

question: How would you conduct yourself when approaching an intersection with a yellow flashing traffic light?
answers: Slow down and even stop if necessary - according to the surrounding traffic.
In any case – stop before the pedestrian crossing.
Speed up before the light turns red.
Slow down and give right-of-way to vehicles coming from your left only.
explanation: A flashing yellow traffic light is a caution signal, not a fixed right-of-way rule for one direction, so drivers must slow down, and stop if the actual traffic situation demands it, using judgment rather than assuming priority.

question: Under which conditions is it permitted to cross railway tracks?
answers: You are only permitted to cross after giving right-of-way to the vehicles that drive away from the crossing, and without causing any disturbance to them.
When a “stop” sign or a “red” traffic light are placed in your direction of driving.
When the barrier starts to lift..
When the railway-crossing is free, with its barrier lifted, and you can be cross it safely.
explanation: Crossing railway tracks is permitted only once the crossing is entirely clear, the barrier is fully raised, and it can be crossed safely; a barrier that has merely started to lift does not yet make the crossing safe.

question: What should you do when you are about to start driving after stopping or parking at the side of the roadway?
answers: You should signal with your left hand and swiftly merge with traffic. .
You should, before starting to drive, signal and then get on the road quickly.
Make a left-signal and drive. The other vehicle should give you right-of-way.
You should signal appropriately and ensure that you can merge with the traffic without endangering other road users.
explanation: Before pulling away from a stop or parking spot, the driver must signal appropriately and actually confirm that merging into traffic will not endanger anyone, rather than assuming the signal alone entitles them to right of way.

question: What should you do when approaching a pedestrian crossing that is being crossed by pedestrians?
answers: Stop and give right-of-way to the pedestrians that cross the road from left to right only.
Slow down, honk and warn the pedestrians that you intend to continue driving.
Speed up and cross in front or behind them, without endangering them.
Always slow down and even stop if required, in order to allow the pedestrians to cross the roadway safely.
explanation: Approaching a pedestrian crossing that people are actively using, a driver must always slow down, and stop if necessary, to let them finish crossing safely, regardless of which direction the pedestrians happen to be moving.

question: How should one refer to a pedestrian crossing that is divided by a traffic island?
answers: The pedestrian crossing should be considered as two separate crossings only when a garden separates between them.
A pedestrian crossing that is divided by a separation area in regarded as one long crossing.
There is no difference between a divided and a non-divided pedestrian crossing. They are both regarded as one crossing.
A pedestrian crossing that is divided by a traffic island shall be regarded as two separate pedestrian crossings.
explanation: A pedestrian crossing split by a traffic island is treated legally as two separate crossings, so a driver must independently give way to pedestrians on each half rather than treating the whole thing as one continuous crossing.

question: What would you do if your driving lane is obstructed?
answers: Quickly cross the obstruction from either its right or left.
Drive slowly and disregard the road signs that are posted in the place.
Cross the obstruction from the right only, and vehicles approaching from your front are supposed to give you right-of-way.
Obey the signals that are given by a policeman, a signaler or a road sign.
explanation: When a driving lane is obstructed, the driver must follow the instructions of a police officer, a signaler, or the relevant road sign for how to proceed around it, rather than deciding alone which side to pass or assuming automatic right of way.

question: What should you do when your driving lane is obstructed?
answers: You should use the horn and cross the obstacle in front.
Go! You have “right of way” in the road that is in front of you.
You should pass through the sidewalk, if it is free.

The vehicle’s side and width projection light should be turned on, unless the road’s lighting is sufficient for observing the vehicle.
The vehicle’s side light should be turned on, and the portable lamp should be flickering.
There is no provision of law for this type of vehicle, but only for over-280-centimeters-wide vehicles.
explanation: A vehicle wider than 210 centimeters needs extra side and width marker lights during lighting time so other drivers can judge its true width in the dark, unless street lighting already makes it clearly visible.

question: In a vehicle that has an overall width of 210 centimeters or more and that is lawfully equipped with side lamps:
answers: The driver must turn-on the side lamps during “light time”.
The driver must turn-on the side lamps in an inter-urban road only.
The driver doesn’t have to turn-on the side lamps during ‘light time”.
It is allowed to drive at any time, even if the side lamps are out of order.
explanation: A vehicle wide enough to be fitted with side lamps must switch them on whenever lighting-time rules apply, so other drivers can gauge its full width in low light.

question: If a vehicle is lawfully photographed while committing an offence, who of the following is held responsible for the offense?
answers: The driver’s employer.
The driver and the passenger besides him.
The vehicle’s owner, unless he proves that the vehicle was driven by another person and he identifies this person.
It is not important. The main thing is to have the fine paid.
explanation: Since a camera identifies only the vehicle and not who was driving, the law defaults responsibility to the registered owner, shifting it only if the owner names the actual driver at the time.

question: When pedestrians are forced to walk on the road way, on which side of it should they walk?
answers: Next to the right “hard shoulder”.
Next to the left sidewalk.
Next to the road’s left edge, when they are facing the incoming traffic.
Next to the road’s right edge.
explanation: Walking facing oncoming traffic on the road's left edge lets pedestrians see approaching vehicles and react in time, which is the basic safety rule when no sidewalk is available.

question: The period that a “new driver” is obliged to be escorted in a private passenger vehicle is?
answers: Two years from the date in which the license was initially received.
Three months from the date in which the license was initially received.
Two months from the date in which the license was initially received.
There is no time limitation as regards to a new-driver escorting period.
explanation: A newly licensed driver must be accompanied by an experienced escort for an initial fixed period of three months to gain supervised experience before driving fully independently.

question: Who is required to have an escort as a ”new driver” while driving a private passenger car?
answers: Anybody receiving for the first time a driver’s license for private passenger cars, and is younger than 30 years of age.
Anybody receiving for the first time a driver’s license for private passenger cars, and is younger than 21 years of age.
Anybody receiving for the first time a driver’s license for private passenger cars or a C1 class license for light trucks.
Anybody receiving for the first time a driver’s license for private passenger cars, and is younger than 24 years of age.
explanation: The escort requirement applies to anyone receiving a first driver's license for private cars or the equivalent light-truck category, since both are new to unsupervised driving.

question: A “new driver” aged less than 21 years (or has not completed two years from the date of receiving a "new driver" license) cannot transport in a vehicle:
answers: More than three passengers, besides himself, unless an escort sits beside him.
More than one person, besides himself.
More than four passengers, besides himself, unless an escort sits beside him.
More than two passengers, besides himself, unless an escort sits beside him in the front seat.
explanation: A new driver under twenty-one, or within two years of first licensing, may carry at most two extra passengers unless an experienced escort sits beside them in the front seat, limiting distraction for an inexperienced driver.

question: In case of a driver incurring 36 demerit points or more:
answers: The Licensing Authority is not authorized to revoke his license based on the point system.
Only a court of law is allowed and authorized to revoke his license.
The Licensing Authority shall revoke his driver’s license for a period of three months and he will be required to undergo a theory exam..
The Licensing Authority may recommend a court of law to permanently revoke his license
explanation: Under the demerit-point thresholds, reaching thirty-six or more points automatically triggers a three-month license suspension plus a required theory exam before the license can be reinstated.

question: The license of a “New driver” will not be renewed as a regular driver's license, if he is convicted of:
answers: Not stopping where a “give right-of–way” signpost is placed.
Illegal overtaking
Not placing a “new driver” sign on the vehicle’s rear window.
Driving a motor vehicle without valid insurance.
explanation: Illegal overtaking is treated as a serious offense reflecting dangerous judgment, so a conviction for it blocks the automatic upgrade of a new driver's license to a regular one.

question: The license of a “New driver” will not be renewed as a regular driver's license, if he is convicted of:
answers: Driving a motor vehicle without valid insurance.
Not placing a warning triangle before a malfunctioning vehicle that stands on the road.
Not stopping in an intersection where a “give right-of–way” signpost is placed.
Driving a motor vehicle under the influence of alcohol or intoxicants.
explanation: Driving under the influence of alcohol or intoxicants is one of the most serious offenses, so a new driver convicted of it is barred from having the license upgraded to a regular license.

question: On which part of a road should a cyclist ride?
answers: As close as possible to the road’s left edge, facing the incoming traffic.
As close as possible to the right hand side of the road.
Where all other vehicles are driving.
It is absolutely forbidden to ride bicycle on any part of a road.
explanation: Cyclists are treated as slower vehicles sharing the roadway, so like other vehicles they must ride as close as possible to the right edge, not against traffic as pedestrians do.

question: Where is it permitted to park LPG (Liquid Petroleum Gas) fuelled vehicles?
answers: In LPG-Vehicle permitted parking lots, according to the directions of the Ministry of Environmental Protection.
In regular parking lots designated for gasoline vehicles.
In parking lots designated for private passenger cars only.
In LPG-Vehicle permitted parking lots, according to the directions of the Vehicle’s importer.
explanation: LPG vehicles carry pressurized flammable gas, so they may only be parked in lots specifically approved and regulated for that fire risk by the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

question: How should a driver involved in traffic accident with casualties conduct himself?
answers: If he is not culpable of the accident and the other driver involved is later held responsible for it, then he shall clear his vehicle away from the roadway.
He shall clear his vehicle away from the roadway to prevent traffic disturbance and call the rescue forces.
He shall clear away from the road and inform the police about the accident.
He shall not move his vehicle, unless instructed to do so by a policeman or if the vehicle had to be used for medical evacuation purposes.
