Slow down and, if necessary, pull into the “hard shoulder” and even stop, to allow the vehicles behind him to overtake safely.
explanation: A driver of an oversize-freight vehicle who cannot be overtaken due to road conditions must slow down and, if necessary, pull onto the hard shoulder or even stop, to let the vehicles behind overtake safely.

question: What is a “semi-trailer”?
answers: A cabin affixed to a trailer.
A vehicle assembled on a chassis as one unit.
A vehicle assembled on a beam chassis.
A vehicle towing a motor vehicle behind it.
explanation: A semi-trailer is legally defined as a cab unit affixed directly to a trailer, distinguishing it from a rigid single-chassis vehicle or one that merely tows another motor vehicle.

question: Define “connected truck”:
answers: A motor vehicle towing another motor vehicle.
A rigid motor vehicle connected to a trailer .
A vehicle for carrying long freights.
A truck tractor connected with a semi-trailer.
explanation: A connected truck is defined as a rigid motor vehicle to which a trailer has been coupled, as distinct from a combination involving a semi-trailer or two motor vehicles towing each other.

question: When driving on a two-way road and visibility is poor:
answers: You should horn while overtaking to warn the overtaken vehicle.
It is permitted to overtake, unless a “no overtaking” sign is placed.
You should turn on the parking lights while overtaking.
It is forbidden to overtake.
explanation: When visibility is poor on a two-way road, overtaking is forbidden outright, since the driver cannot be sure the opposing lane is clear far enough ahead to complete the maneuver safely.

question: Is a tractor permitted to enter a freeway?
answers: Yes, but only during daylight.
No.
Yes, unless it tows a trailer.
Yes.
explanation: A tractor is not permitted to enter a freeway at all, because its low speed and design are incompatible with freeway traffic conditions regardless of daylight or towing status.

question: What is “overall length”:
answers: The general length of the vehicle, from the rear bumper until the center of the front wheel.
The distance between the front and rear edges of the chassis.
The distance between the vehicle’s most frontal point and the vehicle’s rear point.
The distance between the center of the most rear axle and the center of the most frontal axle.
explanation: Overall length is defined as the distance between the vehicle's most forward point and its most rearward point, including any fixed extensions, not just the chassis or axle span.

question: Which type of vehicle is prohibited to overtake another overtaking vehicle?
answers: Motorcycles.
Buses,(not including minibus), commercial vehicles and work vehicles with an all-up weight of more than 3,500 kg.
Motor vehicles with an all-up weight of more than 4,000 kg.
Commercial vehicles and work vehicles with an all-up weight of 3,500 kg or less.
explanation: Buses excluding minibuses, commercial vehicles, and work vehicles with an all-up weight over 3,500 kg are barred from overtaking another vehicle that is itself already overtaking, since two large vehicles occupying the opposing lane at once creates an extreme hazard.

question: In a roadway having at least two lanes in the same direction of driving, which of the following vehicles must enter an intersection from the right of the two lanes?
answers: Commercial vehicles with an all-up weight of 10,000 kg or less.
Commercial vehicles with an all-up weight of more than 4,000 kg.
Motor commercial vehicles with an all-up weight of 6,000 kg or more.
Commercial vehicles and work vehicles with an all-up weight of more than 10,000 kg.
explanation: On a road with at least two lanes in the same direction, commercial and work vehicles with an all-up weight over 10,000 kg must enter an intersection from the rightmost of the two lanes, keeping heavier, less maneuverable vehicles out of the way of general traffic.

question: A driver of a commercial vehicle that transports more then eight passengers and who is obliged to wear glasses or contact lenses must:
answers: Hold an extra pair of the optical instrument, besides the pair he’s wearing.
Hold in the vehicle a spare pair of glasses or lenses apart from the pair he’s wearing.
Verify before driving the regularity and cleanliness of the optical instrument.
Perform a visual acuity test once every six months, according to requirements.
explanation: A driver of a vehicle carrying more than eight passengers who needs glasses or lenses must carry a spare pair in the vehicle in addition to the ones worn, in case the pair being used is lost or damaged mid-journey.

question: Do the obligations and prohibitions which are imposed on commercial vehicles apply also to trucks?
answers: Yes.
No. The obligations and prohibitions which are imposed on commercial vehicles also apply to integral commercial vehicles only.
Yes, except for the obligation to wear a safety belt.
No.
explanation: The obligations and prohibitions that apply to commercial vehicles apply to trucks as well, since a truck falls within the legal category of commercial vehicle for regulatory purposes.

question: What is a “Tachograph”?
answers: A device installed by the vehicle’s owner under in accordance with the importer’s instructions, and traces the number of rounds of the wheels.
A device in a vehicle which has a disc that traces and records time, distance, driving speed and driver work hours.
A device that is installed in a vehicle in accordance with the importer’s instructions and that traces the vehicle’s speed in order to save on fuel.
A device that is installed in a vehicle and that registers vehicle-related technical data and allows the detection of technical malfunctions while driving.
explanation: A tachograph is a device with a disc that records time, distance traveled, driving speed, and driver work hours, used to monitor compliance with rest and driving-time rules.

question: Which vehicle is regarded as a “commercial vehicle”?
answers: All vehicles besides private vehicles and passenger vehicles.
Any vehicle used to support the livelihood of its owner or driver.
A vehicle used or designed to transport freight for hire, for the purpose of the vehicle owner’s business and trade.
Vehicles used to carry goods for hire only.
explanation: A commercial vehicle is legally defined as a vehicle used or designed to transport freight for hire, in connection with the owner's business or trade.

question: A taxi driver that is obliged to wear eyeglasses or any other optical instrument:
answers: Must hold an extra pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses at the taxi station.
Must ensure that he carries on him a pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses while driving during the night.
Must ensure that he carries on him a pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses while driving during the day.
Must carry with him an extra pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses while driving.
explanation: A taxi driver who needs glasses or another optical aid must carry an extra pair with him whenever driving, so that a lost or broken pair doesn't leave him unable to see properly mid-shift.

question: What does the Carrier Service Law determine?
answers: Freight transportation arrangements to and from the port.
The law determines the all up weight of transportation vehicles.
The law determines maximum tariffs for ground transportation.
The law states that transport services by a commercial vehicle with an all up weight exceeding 10,000 kg shall not be provided without a "carrier license".
explanation: The Carrier Service Law establishes that transport services using a commercial vehicle with an all-up weight over 10,000 kg may not be provided without holding a carrier license.

question: Who is required to have a carrier license?
answers: Any provider of transportation services on a commercial vehicle weighing 8,000 kg or less.
Anyone owning more than five passenger transportation vehicles.
Any commercial vehicle.
Any provider of transport services on a commercial vehicle with an all up weight of 10,000 kg or more.
explanation: Anyone providing transport services with a commercial vehicle weighing 10,000 kg or more is required to hold a carrier license under the Carrier Services Law.

question: For what period is a carrier license given?
answers: One year.
Five years.
The length of time depends on the type of freight.
Until the vehicle registration document is renewed.
explanation: A carrier license is issued for a period of one year, after which it must be renewed.

question: What is a commercial vehicle in accordance with the Carrier Services Law?
answers: Any commercial vehicle used for paid transportation only.
Vehicles used for passenger transportation only.
A vehicle with an all up weight of 10,000 kg or more and a vehicle transporting hazardous materials of any weight.
A commercial vehicle, as per its lawful definition, that was given a permit to carry goods and transport passengers.
explanation: Under the Carrier Services Law, a commercial vehicle is one with an all-up weight of 10,000 kg or more, or any vehicle transporting hazardous materials regardless of its weight.

question: A public minibus driver that is obliged to wear eyeglasses or any other optical instrument:
answers: Must hold an extra pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses at the bus station.
Must wear the eyeglasses or the contact lenses while driving – at least during the day.
Must wear the eyeglasses or the contact lenses while driving – at least during the night.
Must hold with him an extra pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses while driving.
explanation: A public minibus driver who requires glasses or lenses must carry a spare pair with him while driving, ensuring he is never left without corrective vision aids affecting his passengers' safety.

question: You are driving a heavy truck down a steep and long descent. When should you shift to an appropriate low gear?
answers: The gears are insignificant for slowing down, but you must use the speed retarders intelligently.
There is no need to shift to low gear. You should shift to high gear and regulate your speed with the speed retarder, to increase safety.
You should shift to low gear towards the end of the descent.
You should shift to low gear at the beginning of the descent.
explanation: On a steep, long descent a driver must shift into a suitably low gear at the very start of the descent, so that engine braking is available throughout rather than only once speed has already built up.

question: What is the risk in shifting gears while driving a heavy vehicle down a steep descent?
answers: There is no risk in shifting gears, and gears are not so important, as long as one of them is operated.
Shifting gears while driving down a steep descent is not dangerous.
There is no danger. By shifting from low gear to high gear while driving on a steep descent, the vehicle can drive faster.
There is a risk that the gear would not shift and the vehicle would stay in neutral gear.
explanation: There is a risk that a heavy vehicle's gear may fail to engage while shifting on a steep descent, leaving it briefly in neutral with no engine braking at all, which is why gear changes on descents must be handled carefully.

question: After connecting a trailer to a towing vehicle or to a truck, is it required to check brake response?
answers: No, there is no need to check the response of the brakes.
Yes, the connection of a trailer or a semi-trailer requires the performance of a brake response check when starting to drive.
Yes, after connecting to a towing vehicle or to a truck tractor, it is required to check the proper functioning of the brakes at a brake-testing facility.
No, the driver doesn’t have the means to check the response of the brakes.
explanation: After coupling a trailer to a towing vehicle, the driver must check that the brakes respond properly before starting to drive, since a faulty connection could leave the trailer's brakes non-functional.

question: When you are driving a truck down a steep descent:
answers: Drive down on high gear and stop the vehicle every few kilometers.
Drive down on neutral gear and use the brakes according to need.
Drive in an appropriate low gear and make sure that the vehicle’s special deceleration mechanisms are operating.
The use of gears to brake the vehicle is of no significance.
explanation: On a steep descent a truck should be driven in an appropriate low gear with its special deceleration mechanisms engaged, using engine braking rather than relying on the service brakes alone to avoid overheating them.

question: What warning measures are installed in the driver’s compartment of a vehicle with a pneumatic braking system (air pressure)?
answers: Warning lamp, warning buzzer, and air pressure gauge.
Red warning lamp in the middle of the dashboard.
Warning lamp and emergency braking handle.
Warning lamp and independent brake.
explanation: A vehicle fitted with a pneumatic air braking system must have a warning lamp, a warning buzzer, and an air-pressure gauge in the driver's compartment, so the driver is alerted if air pressure drops too low for safe braking.

question: What factors affect the stability of a freight-carrying commercial vehicle while driving in a curve?
answers: The weight of the vehicle and of the engine.
The radius and length of the curve.
The vehicle’s speed, the radius of the curve and the height of the vehicle’s center of gravity.
Only the vehicle’s speed and weight.
explanation: The stability of a freight-carrying commercial vehicle in a curve depends on its speed, the curve's radius, and the height of its center of gravity, since these together determine how much centrifugal force is generated relative to the vehicle's tendency to tip or skid.

question: Is  every taxi required to have an ABS anti-lock braking system?
answers: No, only buses and private passenger cars must have it.
No, only buses and commercial vehicles must have it.
No, only city cabs must have it.
Yes.
explanation: Every taxi is required to be equipped with an ABS anti-lock braking system, since taxis carry paying passengers frequently in varied traffic conditions.

question: The higher is the vehicle’s center of gravity:
answers: The higher is the vehicle’s stability on wet roads.
The lesser is the vehicle’s stability in turns and curves.
The easier it is for the vehicle to make turns
The higher is the vehicle’s stability in curves.
explanation: The higher a vehicle's center of gravity, the less stable it is when cornering, since a higher center of gravity increases the tipping and rollover tendency under the centrifugal force generated in a turn.

question: Which of the following road sign prohibits making a left U-turn?
explanation: The pictured sign shows an arrow instructing drivers to continue straight or turn right, while explicitly forbidding a left turn, including a left U-turn, at that point.

question: The manufacure date of a vehicle’s tire is:
answers: Noted in the vehicle book.
Marked on the tire.
Noted in the vehicle’s registration document.
Noted in the vehicle’s insurance policy.
explanation: A tire's manufacture date is molded and marked directly on the tire itself as a date code, not recorded in any vehicle paperwork, since it is a property of that specific tire rather than of the vehicle.

question: How would you connect the truck cabin to the semi-trailer?
answers: By driving backwards at an angle of less than 15 degrees.
By pushing the semi-trailer forward until the truck cabin.
By driving backwards when both of them are aligned in a straight line.
By driving backwards while the cabin is in a diagonal angle or any other comfortable angle..
explanation: A truck cab should be connected to a semi-trailer by reversing straight back while both are aligned in a single straight line, ensuring the fifth-wheel coupling engages correctly and safely.

question: What risk is a rigid vehicle with trailer or a semi-trailer truck expected to face while driving on a slippery roadway?
answers: On a slippery road all vehicles are at risk, and a connected vehicle or a semi-trailer truck is not special in this sense.
The vehicle can skid into a “jack-knife” position, in which a large angle is formed between the trailer and the towing vehicle,
Loss of engine power due to the slippage of a long vehicle.
That the deceleration brake stops functioning.
explanation: On a slippery road, a connected vehicle or semi-trailer truck risks entering a jack-knife position, where the trailer swings out at a sharp angle relative to the towing unit because the trailer's wheels lose grip and slide.

question: On an inter-urban road without a centre dividing area, what is the speed limit for a commercial vehicle with an all up weight that doesn’t exceed 3.5 tons (if not indicated otherwise by any road sign)?
explanation: On an interurban road without a center divider, a commercial vehicle up to 3.5 tons is limited to 80 km/h by default, matching the standard speed table for that vehicle class absent a different posted sign.

question: It is permitted to park a service route bus (not for the purpose of passenger loading / unloading):
answers: According to the provisions of the route license, if such was determined by the Authority.
In every bus station.
In any place, according to the passengers’ request.
In every public parking lot.
explanation: A service-route bus may only be parked, other than for loading or unloading passengers, according to what its route license permits, since deviating from the licensed route or stops without authorization is not allowed.

question: On an urban road, what is the speed limit (in k.p.h) for a commercial vehicle with an all up weight of more than 12,000 kg?
answers: 50 k.p.h.- even if there is a road sign permitting to drive at a higher speed.
50 k.p.h.- if there is a road sign permitting to drive at a higher speed, the vehicle is permitted to drive at the speed indicated in the sign.
60 k.p.h.- even if there is a road sign permitting to drive at a higher speed.
60 k.p.h.- if there is a road sign permitting to drive at a higher speed, the vehicle is permitted to drive at the speed indicated in the sign.
explanation: On an urban road a commercial vehicle over 12,000 kg is capped at 50 km/h even if a sign permits a higher speed, because the statutory weight-based limit for heavy vehicles overrides a general posted urban speed sign.

question: What is the maximum freight weight a commercial vehicle is permitted to carry?
answers: The freight’s weight should not exceed the weight that was determined by the vehicle’s manufacturer.
The freight’s weight should not exceed the permitted weight that is indicated in the vehicle’s registration document.
The freight’s weight would be the weight determined by the vehicle’s manufacturer plus no more than 50%.
The freight’s weight would be in accordance with the vehicle’s tire manufacturer only.
explanation: The maximum freight weight a commercial vehicle may carry is the weight specified as permitted in that vehicle's registration document, not a value set independently by the manufacturer or tire supplier.

question: What is the legal definition of a "-trailer"?
answers: A motorized trailer with a frontal part that rests on a towing vehicle.
A motor vehicle that is designed to be towed by another vehicle.
A trailer that has its front part resting on the support surface behind a cab.
A trailer that has its rear part supported by a cab.
explanation: A trailer is legally defined as a unit whose front part rests on the support surface located behind a cab, distinguishing it from a full trailer that carries its own front axle.

question: What might be the effect of sand scattered on the road?
answers: Vehicle skidding, due to reduced friction between the tires and the road.
Tire overheating, due to increased friction between the tires and the road.
Better braking force, due to increased friction between the tires and the road.
It might conceal important road signs.
explanation: Sand scattered on the road reduces the friction between tires and the road surface, making the vehicle prone to skidding, especially under braking or cornering.

question: Which of these traffic signs permits bicycle entry?
explanation: The pictured sign designates a path reserved for bicycles, permitting bicycle entry onto that dedicated path.

question: A person shall not, and shall not permit anybody, to transport a freight container on his vehicle, unless:
answers: The vehicle has an engine of at least 150 horse-powers.
The vehicle’s all up weight is at least 14,000 kg.
The vehicle has two spare tires.
It is indicated in the vehicle’s registration document that the vehicle is permitted to transport freight containers.
explanation: A freight container may only be transported on a vehicle if its registration document explicitly states that the vehicle is approved to carry freight containers, since the vehicle's chassis and fittings must be certified for that use.

question: It is obligatory to install on the rear of a commercial vehicle with an all up weight of 12,000 kg or more:
answers: Two white light reflecting strips.
Two rectangular tables colored in red/white.
Two triangular yellow-light reflectors colored in red/white.
Two round yellow-light reflectors, colored in red/white.
explanation: A commercial vehicle with an all-up weight of 12,000 kg or more must have two red and white rectangular reflective plates mounted on its rear, making the outline of the large vehicle clearly visible to traffic approaching from behind.

question: When is a vehicle affected by centrifugal force?
answers: While driving in a straight line, even when the road is horizontal.
While driving around curves and turns.
While driving straight in steep uphill climbs.
While driving straight in steep descents.
explanation: Centrifugal force acts on a vehicle while it is driving around curves and turns, pushing it outward from the turning path in proportion to speed and inversely to the curve's radius.

question: How is it possible to reduce the centrifugal force applied to the vehicle whilst driving?
answers: The effect of these force cannot be reduced – it depends on the vehicle’s size only.
By driving faster.
By driving lawfully and always giving right of way.
By reducing speed.on corners and curves
explanation: Centrifugal force in a turn increases with the square of the speed, so the most effective way to reduce it is to reduce speed before and through corners and curves.

question: After how many hours of rest is a driver of a commercial vehicle with an all up weight of 10,000 kg or more permitted to start working?
answers: After a continuous break of 5 hours.
After a continuous break of 6 hours.
After a continuous rest break of 7 hours.
After a continuous break of 4 hours.
explanation: A driver of a commercial vehicle weighing 10,000 kg or more must take a continuous rest break of at least 7 hours before being permitted to resume work, under the driving-hours rest regulations for heavy-vehicle drivers.

question: Why is it required to drive in low gear on a steep descent?
answers: To save fuel and to reduce engine wear.
To use the engines compression in order to maintain a slow and constant driving speed without overusing the brakes.
To prevent tire wear.
To prevent overheating of the vehicle’s engine.
explanation: Driving in low gear on a steep descent uses the engine's compression to hold a slow, steady speed without relying continuously on the service brakes, which would otherwise overheat and lose effectiveness.

question: While overtaking or passing by another vehicle:
answers: It is permitted to pass the speed limit for a moment, if necessary.
You should drive precisely at the same speed as the overtaken vehicle.
It is prohibited to drive over the speed limit.
You should drive 10 k.p.h slower than the overtaken vehicle.
explanation: A driver may never exceed the posted speed limit while overtaking, even briefly, since exceeding the limit is prohibited regardless of the maneuver being performed.

question: What are the vehicle's “emergency lights”?
answers: The simultaneous flashing of all the vehicle’s indicators.
Warning light placed on the vehicle’s roof.
Warning triangle with lights on it.
Additional brake light at the height of the window.
explanation: A vehicle's emergency lights, or hazard lights, are the simultaneous flashing of all four turn indicators together, used to warn other road users of a hazard or a stopped or slow-moving vehicle.

question: What is the speed limit on an urban road for a private passenger car (if not indicated otherwise by any road sign)?
explanation: The default speed limit for a private passenger car on an urban road, absent any sign stating otherwise, is 50 km/h under the standard speed-limit table.

question: Is a driver permitted to drive over the speed limit while overtaking?
answers: Yes, when it is required in order to shorten the overtaking time.
No.
Yes, but only on a non-urban road.
Yes, but only on a multi-lane road and for a short time.
explanation: A driver may never exceed the posted speed limit while overtaking, even to shorten the time spent in the opposing lane, since the speed limit itself is not suspended during an overtaking maneuver.

question: What is the meaning of a “vehicle non-use notice” (taking a vehicle off the road)?
answers: It is permitted to drive the vehicle up to one week after it is taken off the road.
It is prohibited to drive the vehicle without an authorization from the insurance company.
The vehicle is prohibited from driving, unless it is permitted, according to the non-use form, to drive to a nearby garage.
It is permitted to drive the vehicle unlimitedly (if it doesn’t cause any traffic safety risk) but not on road ways.
explanation: A vehicle non-use notice takes the vehicle off the road entirely; it may only be driven if the non-use form itself permits a specific trip, such as to a nearby garage, and not otherwise.

question: The reaction distance depends on:
answers: The vehicle’s speed only.
The driver’s response only.
The driver’s reaction time and the vehicle’s speed.
The proper function of the vehicle's brakes.
explanation: Reaction distance depends on both the driver's reaction time and the vehicle's speed, since a slower reaction or a higher speed each independently lengthens the distance traveled before any braking begins.

question: The reaction distance is the distance covered by the vehicle:
answers: From the moment the driver eases off his step on the accelerator until the vehicle stops.
From the moment the driver notices the danger until he starts to apply the action he decided to take.
From the moment the driver steps on the brakes until the vehicle stops.
From the moment the driver notices the danger until the vehicle makes a complete stop.
explanation: Reaction distance is the distance the vehicle covers from the moment the driver notices a hazard until they begin to act on it, during which no braking or steering control action has yet taken effect.

question: What is the correct sentence?
answers: The braking distance is always longer than the reaction distance.
The reaction distance is always longer than the braking distance.
The braking distance is always longer that the stopping distance.
The stopping distance is always longer than the braking distance.
explanation: The total stopping distance, reaction distance plus braking distance, is always longer than the braking distance alone, since braking distance is only one component of the full distance needed to stop.

question: You are driving on a two-way road and in front of you drives a vehicle that signals with its left indicator:
answers: You may immediately overtake it from its right, by pulling into the “hard shoulder”.
You should take into consideration that the vehicle before you might deviate to the left and you should allow it to do so.
You shouldn’t overtake it on a narrow roadway, but you may overtake it from its left side on a wide road.
You may overtake after using the horn to warn him. The signal he gives doesn’t oblige you.
explanation: When a vehicle ahead signals a left turn on a two-way road, you should assume it may indeed move left and let it do so, since a driver must always account for another vehicle's signaled intentions under the general duty of care.

question: When visibility on the road is poor, the driver should:
answers: Slow down, adjust his speed to the visibility conditions and turn-on his dipped beam.
On a two-way road – slow down; and on a one-way road – continue driving normally.
Accelerate and turn-on the rear lights, to prevent collision with the vehicle driving behind.
Turn-on the high beam to extend the field of vision and warn the incoming traffic from your opposite direction.
explanation: When visibility is poor, a driver must slow down, adjust speed to match the reduced visibility, and turn on the dipped low-beam headlights so that both the driver and others can see and be seen.

question: Who is permitted to transport hazardous materials?
answers: Anybody who was trained to do it and obtained a permit from the body that trained him.
Anybody who successfully completed a heavy vehicle driving course.
Anybody who is permitted to drive a vehicle with an all up weight of more than 12,000 kg..
Only someone who was trained to do so and obtained a permit from the Ministry of Transportation.
explanation: Only a person trained and holding a permit issued by the Ministry of Transportation is authorized to transport hazardous materials, since specialized knowledge of handling and emergency procedures is required.

question: Under what terms is it permitted to transport hazardous materials?
answers: The transportation should be approved by the Ministry of Internal Security.
The driver must have an adequate permit, and the vehicle must be new (less than four years).
A vehicle transporting a hazardous material must have a gasoline engine only.
The driver and the vehicle must have adequate permits to transport hazardous materials from the Licensing Authority.
explanation: Transporting hazardous materials requires that both the driver and the vehicle hold the appropriate permits issued by the Licensing Authority, since both the person's training and the vehicle's suitability must be certified.

question: How should a driver conduct himself after hitting a parked vehicle in the absence of its owners?
answers: Leave a note on the vehicle he hit with his personal details, the details of his vehicle and his insurance policy, and report to the police within 24 hours.
Wait until a representative of his insurance company arrives and report to the police within 48 hours.
Inform about the accident to the police station within 7 days.
Wait at the place until the owner of the vehicle arrives.
explanation: After hitting a parked vehicle whose owner is absent, the driver must leave a note with personal, vehicle, and insurance details at the scene and report the incident to the police within 24 hours, fulfilling the duty to identify oneself when the other party isn't present.

question: The distance covered by a vehicle from the moment we step on the brake pedal until the vehicle stops becomes bigger:
answers: The faster we drive.
The longer is the response time.
The slower we drive.
The newer is the vehicle.
explanation: The distance a vehicle travels from the moment the brake pedal is pressed until it stops increases the faster the vehicle is being driven, since braking distance grows with the square of the speed.

question: To disconnect the engine from the wheels, you should:
answers: Press the clutch pedal.
Step on the brake pedal and on the accelerator.
Shut-off the engine.
Press on the starter switch.
explanation: Pressing the clutch pedal disengages the engine from the wheels by disconnecting the drivetrain, allowing gear changes or the vehicle to coast without engine power being transmitted.

question: What should a driver verify before lifting his car to change a wheel?
answers: He must ensure, in all possible ways that the vehicle cannot move.
That the auxiliary (parking/hand) is secured until the wheel is taken off, and then released while the new wheel is installed.
That the auxiliary (parking/hand) brake is released until the wheel is taken off, and then tightened while the new wheel is installed.
That the auxiliary (parking/hand) is free and released, and that the vehicle is in low gear during the entire course of the wheel change.
explanation: Before lifting a vehicle to change a wheel, the driver must ensure by every possible means that the vehicle cannot move, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked, and gear engaged, since a car rolling off a jack is extremely dangerous.

question: What type of insurance covers the damage that is caused to other vehicles?
answers: Directors insurance.
Third party insurance.
Fire insurance.
Obligatory insurance.
explanation: Third-party insurance is the coverage that pays for damage caused to other vehicles or property, as distinct from coverage for the insured's own vehicle.

question: The depth of the grooves in a tire (pneumatic-air pressure) which comes in contact with the road should not be less than:
answers: 2mm, excluding the spare tire.
2cm, including the spare tire.
2cm, excluding the spare tire.
2mm, including the spare tire.
explanation: Traffic regulations require every tire in use, including the spare, to keep at least 2 mm of tread depth, since worn tread on any wheel, even one held in reserve for emergency use, reduces road grip and stopping ability.

question: A driver of a vehicle carrying oversize freight that cannot be overtaken by other drivers is obliged to:
answers: Continue driving at normal speed, on the right side of the road. He is prohibited to pull down to the “hard shoulders”.
Slow down, if possible, cross the road’s edge and even stop on the “hard shoulder”.
Drive faster, so he doesn’t disturb the vehicles behind him.
Stop his vehicle and signal to the other vehicles to pass him by.
explanation: A vehicle carrying oversize freight that blocks faster traffic must not obstruct following vehicles; the driver is required to ease toward the shoulder and even stop there when needed so others can safely pass.

question: The wind resistance that a driving vehicle faces affects:
answers: The vehicle’s speed and tire wear.
The wear and tear of the steering wheel system,
The capacity of the vehicle’s brakes.
The vehicle’s stability and speed.
explanation: Aerodynamic drag opposes the vehicle's forward motion and can unbalance it, so wind resistance is primarily a stability and speed factor rather than one affecting brakes or steering wear.

question: How would we attach a freight container to the vehicle’s loading surface?
answers: With steel cables – if a screw anchor (twist lock) is absent.
With the walls of the loading surface.
With a screw anchor (twist lock) only.
With two independent chains, each connected to the loading surface.
explanation: Freight containers are engineered to be secured to a loading platform exclusively through their corner castings using screw anchors (twist locks); other attachment methods do not meet the securing standard.

question: Is it permitted to transport a freight container while few of its twist locks are not secured?
answers: Absolutely not.
Yes, but only when transporting short containers.
Yes, but only with the approval of a police officer.
Yes, when transporting a 40 feet container.
explanation: All twist locks on a container must be engaged before the vehicle moves, because even a few unsecured locks let the container shift or detach under braking or cornering forces, so partial securing is never permitted.

question: Where would you load heavy freight on a truck’s freight platform?
answers: The positioning of the heavy freight is non-significant.
From the rear axle to the direction of the driver’s compartment.
In the front part of the freight trunk.
Behind the rear axle.
explanation: Weight-distribution rules require heavy freight to sit toward the front, between the rear axle and the cab, so the load is properly supported over the axles and does not overload or unbalance the rear of the vehicle.

question: What road sign permits entry to pedetrians?
answers: All the signs.
explanation: Sign 226 is the blue instructional sign marking a path reserved for pedestrians, so it is the sign that grants pedestrians permission to enter that route.

question: What are the dangers of driving continuously for many hours?
answers: Heating and accelerated wear of the vehicle’s tires.
Overheating of the vehicle’s engine.
It violates the insurance law.
Tiredness and risk of falling asleep at the wheel
explanation: Extended, uninterrupted driving is the classic cause of fatigue, and fatigue is dangerous specifically because it can lead to microsleeps or fully falling asleep at the wheel.

question: How can we overcome the problem of tiredness while driving?
answers: Have an adequate rest before driving and take rest breaks during the journey.
A short break and a heavy meal will drive the tiredness away for a long time.
Drive slowly until the tiredness passes away.
Physical exercise will drive the tiredness away for many hours.
explanation: Because fatigue cannot be reversed by any driving technique, the only real countermeasure is prevention: sleeping enough before the trip and stopping for genuine rest breaks along the way.

question: Can a refreshment break whilst driving lessen the driver’s tiredness?
answers: It can drive the tiredness away completely.
Yes, for a long time.
Absolutely yes, and it is even better, on the long run, than taking a rest outside the vehicle.
Yes, for a short time.
explanation: A roadside break only postpones tiredness briefly; it is not a substitute for real rest, so its effect on alertness lasts a short time rather than removing fatigue completely.

question: What are the risks of driving a long commercial vehicle?
answers: Inability to turn left safely.
It is not riskier to drive a long vehicle compared to a private passenger car.
The driver’s response time is longer.
Presence of small vehicles within its “blind spots”, and difficulty to make sharp turns.
explanation: Long commercial vehicles have extensive areas around them that the driver cannot see in mirrors or by looking, and their length also limits how sharply they can turn, both of which create extra collision risk.

question: Is a motorcyclist permitted to drive at the side of another motorcycle?
answers: No, he is only permitted to drive at the side of a private passenger car.
No, he is only permitted to drive at the side of a commercial vehicle transporting passengers.
No, but he is permitted to overtake it.
Absolutely not.
explanation: Two-wheeled vehicles must travel one behind the other rather than side by side; riding level with another motorcycle is allowed only momentarily while completing an overtaking maneuver.

question: Up to which height is it permitted to load loose materials?
answers: Up to the height of the rear door of the freight trunk.
Up to the height of the walls of the truck, including the vehicle’s ladders.
Up to the height of the rear window of the driver’s compartment.
Up to the height of the walls of the freight trunk, excluding the vehicle’s ladders.
explanation: Loose bulk materials may only be loaded up to the height of the truck body's side walls, and any built-in ladders or extensions attached to those walls count toward that height limit.

question: Towing without a designated safety pin and without safety chains would cause:
answers: Disengagement of the trailer from the towing vehicle.
Fracture of the towing pin.
Excessive wear of the towing shaft.
Faster and safer harnessing of the trailer.
explanation: A safety pin and safety chains are the backup that keeps a trailer attached if the main coupling fails; without them, a coupling failure lets the trailer separate completely from the towing vehicle.

question: What are the “blind spots”?
answers: Elements obstructing the driver’s rear view.
The areas around a vehicle in which its driver cannot notice other road users – neither by looking nor by glancing at the mirrors.
The area in front of the vehicle only in which the driver can spot pedestrians.
The area behind the vehicle only in which the driver cannot notice other vehicles - neither by looking nor by glancing at the mirrors or by any other means.
explanation: Blind spots are defined as all the zones around the vehicle, not just to the rear, where a road user can be present without the driver being able to detect them by direct sight or through any mirror.

question: Where is the biggest “blind spot” in a commercial vehicle?
answers: It depends on the size of the vehicle’s rear view mirror: The larger it is, the bigger is the dead spot in front.
On the vehicle’s left side.
At the vehicle’s rear.
On the vehicle’s front.
explanation: Because the cargo body blocks the driver's rear-facing sightline and mirrors cannot fully compensate, the largest blind zone on a commercial vehicle is directly behind it.

question: Which vehicles can you drive with class B ?
answers: Private vehicles and commercial vehicles with an all up weight of up to 4,500 kg.
Private vehicles and commercial vehicles with an all up weight of up to 3,500 kg.
Public vehicles, including minibuses.
Motorcycles with an engine power of up to 14.6 horse-powers.
explanation: Licensing rules define Class B as covering private cars and commercial vehicles up to a gross weight of 3,500 kg; heavier commercial vehicles or buses require a higher license class.

question: What effective solution for tiredness is available to the driver?
answers: Turning on the fog lights.
Stopping and resting.
Adjusting the speed to his level of tiredness (driving slower the more tired he is).
Turning on the wipers and solving a cryptic crossword.
explanation: Since fatigue is only relieved by actual rest, the effective solution when tired is to stop driving and rest, not to compensate by changing speed or using cabin controls.

question: What is the meaning of the sign?
answers: End of parking area.
End of area where parking is not permitted.
Beginning of parking area for payment.
Beginning of parking for bicycles only.
explanation: The pictured sign is the cancellation version of a parking-permission sign, posted where a marked parking zone terminates, so it tells drivers the designated parking area has ended.

question: It is obligatory to hold two safety shoes in commercial vehicles with an all up weight that exceeds:
explanation: Regulations require commercial vehicles above 5,000 kg gross weight to carry two safety shoes (wheel chocks), since heavier vehicles need extra wheel-locking protection when parked, especially on slopes.

question: What is the all up length of a commercial vehicle towing a trailer?
answers: 12.75 meters.
16 meters.
18.75 meters.
14 meters.
explanation: Traffic regulations cap the total combined length of a commercial vehicle towing a trailer at 18.75 meters, to keep the combination maneuverable and safe on the road.

question: How is it required to mark freight that sticks out from the vehicle’s front side?
answers: With a white-reflecting triangle on the tip of the oversize freight.
With a red light-reflecting triangle on the tip of the oversize freight.
With a light and a red flag on the tip of the oversize freight.
With a light and a white or yellow flag on the tip of the oversize freight.
explanation: Regulations require freight that projects beyond the front of a vehicle to be marked at its tip with a white reflective triangle, so oncoming and other drivers can see the extended edge, especially at night.

question: When a driver approaches a narrow bridge, he should:
answers: Cross the bridge as quickly as possible, to allow vehicles coming from the opposite direction to pass it without delays.
Slow down while approaching and crossing the bridge.
Stop before the bridge for safety reasons and then cross it quickly.
Drive faster only while approaching the bridge, and drive slowly on the bridge – in order to enhance safety.
explanation: A narrow bridge restricts maneuvering space and may only allow one direction of traffic at a time, so a driver must reduce speed both approaching and while crossing it to stay in control.

question: Which of the following commercial vehicles must be equipped with an                    auxiliary brake?
answers: Commercial vehicles with an all up weight exceeding 4,000 kg.
Commercial vehicles with an all up weight exceeding 6,000 kg.
Commercial vehicles with an all up weight exceeding 5,000 kg.
Diesel-engine vehicles with an all up weight exceeding 8,000 kg.
explanation: Because heavy diesel vehicles need extra stopping capability on long descents, regulations require an auxiliary engine/exhaust brake once the vehicle's gross weight exceeds 8,000 kg.

question: Is it permitted to drive under the influence of sedatives?
answers: Only if the driver tends to be influenced by a certain medication.
Yes, sedatives have no affect on driving.
It is permitted to take sedation pills half an hour before driving.
Not if it is specifically indicated in the prescription or by the doctor.
explanation: Driving under sedatives is only prohibited when a doctor or the medication's label specifically warns against driving, since some sedatives impair reaction time and alertness enough to make safe driving impossible.

question: The length of a commercial vehicles shall not exceed:
answers: 12.5 meters.
10 meters.
12 meters.
11 meters.
explanation: Traffic regulations set the maximum permitted length of a single commercial vehicle, not towing a trailer, at 12 meters, to keep the vehicle stable and maneuverable.

question: What is the maximum permitted height - above the road’s surface -for a loaded commercial vehicle with an all up weight of between 3,501 and 8,000 kg?
answers: 3.50 meters.
4.00 meters.
3.00 meters.
2.50 meters.
explanation: For a loaded commercial vehicle weighing between 3,501 and 8,000 kg, the regulations cap the overall height above the road at 3.50 meters so it can safely clear bridges, tunnels, and overhead obstacles.

question: What should you do when driving on a narrow roadway and you are suddenly approached by a vehicle from the opposite direction?
answers: Honk and signal with your hands for the driver to return to his lane.
Slow down and swerve as far to the right as possible, but don’t pull off the road.
Slow down, move as far to the right as possible and, if necessary, pull off the road.
Turn on your high beam and signal the other driver to return to his lane.
explanation: On a narrow roadway, a driver confronted by an oncoming vehicle must reduce speed and give way by moving right, even leaving the roadway if that is the only way to avoid a head-on collision.

question: How would you drive on a wet road?
answers: Accelerate until the end of the wet section – in order to enhance safety.
Step on the clutch pedal intermittently.
Slow down and drive at a reasonable speed, according to the road conditions.
The same as on a dry road. There is no difference.
explanation: Regulation 51 requires speed to always be reasonable for the actual road and traffic conditions, and since wet roads reduce tire grip and lengthen braking distance, a reasonable speed on them is necessarily lower than on a dry road.

question: When entering a curve and driving through it a driver is required to:
answers: Accelerate at the entry to the curve and slow down in the middle of it.
Accelerate to ensure smooth turning.
Slow down and maintain a constant speed
Stay close to the middle of the roadway to ensure vehicle stability.
explanation: Braking or accelerating while a vehicle is turning shifts the tires' grip away from cornering, increasing skid risk, so the safe technique is to slow before the curve and hold a steady speed through it.

question: When you are driving behind another vehicle:
answers: While driving uphill – keep a small distance; while driving downhill – keep double distance.
Keep a safe distance from the vehicle in front of you, to prevent an accident.
Keep a smaller distance from the vehicle in front of you.
Keep a larger distance from the vehicle in front of you only when a “general danger” road sign is placed.
explanation: Regulation 49(a) requires a driver to maintain a gap from the vehicle ahead that leaves room to stop and avoid a collision, which is why keeping a safe distance is the correct rule regardless of grade or road markings.

question: How is the required distance for overtaking determined?
answers: It only depends on the driving speed of the overtaken vehicle and not of the overtaking one.
It depends on the driving speeds of the overtaking and the overtaken vehicles
It only depends on the driving speed of the overtaking vehicle and not of the overtaken one.
It corresponds to the speed limit in that road section.
explanation: The distance needed to complete an overtake depends on the relative closing speed between the two vehicles, so both the overtaking vehicle's speed and the overtaken vehicle's speed determine how much distance the maneuver requires.

question: How many vehicles is it permitted to tow by a commercial vehicle with an all up weight exceeding 2,200 kg?
answers: Two vehicles.
One vehicle, unless approved otherwise by the Licensing Authority.
Only a tractor is permitted to tow another vehicle. A small commercial vehicle is prohibited to do so.
There is no restriction on the number of vehicles that can be towed.
explanation: A commercial vehicle over 2,200 kg is limited by regulation to towing a single vehicle at a time, unless the Licensing Authority has specifically approved towing more.

question: What should a vehicle driver do in case of a strong side wind?
answers: Slow down and adjust the driving speed to allow him to control the vehicle – .
He should avoid driving on roads with side winds, or he should otherwise stop on the “hard shoulders” until the wind fades.
Turn on the fog lights and continue driving normally.
Drive faster to avoid the side wind.
explanation: A strong side wind pushes against the vehicle and can destabilize it, so reducing speed to a level where the driver retains full steering control is the required response.

question: What sign forbids entry to pedestrians?
explanation: Sign 216 marks the entrance to an expressway, a road category from which pedestrians, along with animals and slow vehicles, are legally excluded, which is why this sign effectively forbids pedestrian entry.

question: How is a driver required to conduct himself when a vehicle stops before him on approaching a pedestrian crossing?
answers: He is prohibited from overtaking the vehicle that stopped before the crossing.
He is permitted to overtake if the pedestrian crossing has a traffic light.
He is permitted to overtake the vehicle that stopped before the crossing.
He is prohibited to overtake the other vehicle on an urban road only.
explanation: A vehicle stopped before a pedestrian crossing may be yielding to a pedestrian hidden from the following driver's view, so overtaking it is prohibited to avoid striking a pedestrian who cannot yet be seen.

question: It is obligatory to assign an escorting vehicle to commercial vehicles carrying oversize freight with a width that exceeds:
answers: 3 meters.
20 cm from each side of the vehicle’s freight trunk.
2.5 meters.
3.40 meters.
explanation: Once a load's width exceeds 3.40 meters, regulations require an escorting vehicle to accompany the oversize load, since a width beyond this threshold poses a heightened risk to other traffic that needs extra warning.

question: How is it required to mark freight that sticks out from the vehicle’s rear side?
answers: With a red light-reflecting triangle on the tip of the oversize freight.
With a white light-reflecting triangle on the tip of the oversize freight.
With a white or yellow light on the tip of the oversize freight.
With a red light on the tip of the oversize freight.
explanation: Freight overhanging the rear of a vehicle must be marked with a red reflective triangle at its tip, since red is the standard rear warning color so following drivers recognize the projecting hazard, especially in low light.

question: How is it required to mark freight that sticks out from the vehicle’s rear side?
answers: With a white flag tied to the tip of the oversize freight.
With a red light-reflecting triangle. The length of each triangle side should be 60cm.
With a white light-reflecting triangle. The length of each triangle side should be 60cm.
With a red flag tied to the tip of the oversize freight.
explanation: The regulation for marking rearward-projecting freight specifies not only a red reflective triangle but also its exact size, 60 cm per side, so the marker is large enough to be seen clearly from a safe distance.

question: “Reasonable speed” is a speed:
answers: That is adjusted to the road conditions and circumstances and does not exceed the speed limit.
The speed limit on that road, under all circumstances.
That the vehicle passengers wish to drive at. The passengers are always right.
That is adjusted to the conditions and circumstances, and always exceeds speed limit.
explanation: Regulation 51 defines 'reasonable speed' as one suited to the actual road, traffic, and weather conditions, and this speed can never exceed the posted legal limit even when conditions would otherwise allow faster driving.

question: How many years after its manufature will a license of a towing vehicle not be renewed?
answers: 19 years.
15 years.
11 years.
23 years.
explanation: Regulations set a maximum service life for towing-vehicle licensing, and once a towing vehicle reaches 19 years from its manufacture date its license may no longer be renewed, reflecting the greater wear of older heavy vehicles.

question: Driving at dark with the high beam turned on might:
answers: Waste electricity.
Blind (dazzle) other drivers.
Spoil the battery.
Impair the driver’s vision.
explanation: High beams project a strong, high-angle light that can shine directly into the eyes of oncoming or leading drivers, temporarily impairing their vision, which is the dazzling effect Regulation 99(a) requires drivers to prevent.

question: Is it permitted to drive on the sidewalk in order to pass a road obstacle?
answers: Yes. It is permitted to bypass the obstacle only through the sidewalk, if it is simpler.
Yes. It is permitted to drive on the sidewalk very carefully and in first gear.
No. It is prohibited to drive on the sidewalk in order to pass an obstacle.
Yes. It is permitted to drive on the sidewalk, but only if the roadway is in a bad condition.
explanation: Sidewalks are reserved for pedestrians, so bypassing a road obstacle by driving onto one is prohibited regardless of how carefully it is done or how bad the roadway condition is.

question: The all up width of a refrigeration unit commercial vehicle should not exceed:
answers: 2.60 meters.
2.50 meters.
3.40 meters.
2.55 meters.
explanation: Refrigerated, insulated truck bodies are permitted a slightly greater overall width, up to 2.60 meters, than the standard 2.50 meter limit, to account for the extra wall thickness needed for insulation.

question: What is the legal definition of a trailer?
answers: A motor vehicle that is intended to be towed behind a motor vehicle.
A motorized trailer with a frontal part resting against the support surface of a towing vehicle.
A non-motorized vehicle that is intended to be towed behind a motor vehicle.
The legal definitions of a trailer and a semit-trailer are identical.
explanation: The defining legal feature of a trailer is that it has no engine of its own and is built specifically to be towed by a motor vehicle, distinguishing it from a semi-trailer or a motorized towed unit.

question: What is the duty of a driver after sensing that some of the freight he is carrying had fallen-onto the roadway
answers: Inform about it to the police. The municipality or the Public Works Department is responsible to clear it away.
Inform the insurance company.
Inform the police and the insurance company.
Stop immediately, and make sure that the falling freight is cleared away immediately.
explanation: A driver who creates a hazard on the roadway by spilling freight is responsible for removing that hazard right away, so the duty is to stop at once and ensure the fallen freight is cleared, not merely to report it.

question: Sudden braking is permitted when:
answers: It is the only way to prevent an accident.
The driver or any of the passengers suddenly want to get off the vehicle.
The driver wants to make a U-turn.
The driver realizes he is lost.
explanation: Sudden braking is generally discouraged because it endangers following traffic, so it is only justified when it is genuinely the sole means available to avoid a collision.

question: When you exit a dirt road on to a paved road.
answers: There is no obligation to give right of way. It depends on the good will of the driver exiting the dirt road.
Give right of way to vehicle traffic on the roadway only when it is a two-way roadway.
Give right of way to vehicles coming from your right side only and then drive. Incoming traffic from your left side should yield.
Give right of way to vehicle traffic on the paved road from all directions.
explanation: An unpaved dirt road is always treated as the lower-priority road at its junction with a paved road, so a driver exiting onto the paved road must yield to paved-road traffic coming from every direction, not just one side.

question: Who should verify that a bus is equipped with a complete set of first aid equipment?
answers: The owner of the bus.
The bus driver is obliged to verify that the equipment is present, but only when the bus comes out of the garage for the first time after being repaired.
The bus driver must verify that this equipment is always on the bus.
The manager of the company’s garage has to verify that this equipment is present on the bus at all times.
explanation: Responsibility for a bus's roadworthiness, including having complete first aid equipment on board at all times, rests continuously with the driver, not only at the point the bus leaves the garage.

question: What is a driver required to do when he feels tired during night-driving?
answers: Search for a safe place to rest and take a light nap where he doesn’t disturb traffic.
Listen to the radio, but avoid relaxing music.
Open the window next to him, to allow air flow in.
Eat a heavy meal and avoid drinking.
explanation: Because fatigue while driving at night is a genuine danger, the required response is to find a safe spot off the flow of traffic and rest, rather than trying to power through with distractions or stimulants.

question: In a work vehicle:
answers: It is prohibited to transport passengers but it is permitted to carry freight.
It is prohibited to carry freight but it is permitted to carry up to 6 passengers in the vehicle’s trunk.
It is permitted to transport passengers and to carry freight.
It is prohibited to carry freight or transport passengers, except in the driver’s compartment.
explanation: A work vehicle is licensed for its specific work function, not as freight or passenger transport, so regulations prohibit carrying freight or passengers anywhere on it apart from seats in the driver's own compartment.

question: Is it permitted to drive under the influence of an intoxicating alcoholic drink?
answers: Yes, provided that the driver doesn’t mix drinks.
Absolutely not.
Yes, but only after family gatherings and for short distances.
Yes, it is permitted.
explanation: Driving under the influence of alcohol is an absolute prohibition in traffic law, with no exception for amount consumed, occasion, or distance driven.

question: It is permitted to park, stop or stand a vehicle when the distance between the vehicle’s wheels and the road’s edge doesn’t exceed:
answers: 80 cm.
50 cm.
60 cm.
40 cm.
explanation: Regulations permit parking, standing, or stopping only when the vehicle's wheels are within 40 cm of the road's edge, keeping the vehicle close enough to the side to avoid obstructing the traveled lane.

question: When spending time in a club (pub):
answers: It should be planned to wait one hour after leaving the pub, and then there should be no danger to drive.
It should be agreed that the person drinking the least amount of alcohol would drive after leaving the pub.
A designated driver, who abstains from drinking alcohol, should be determined in advance.
It should be agreed that the most experienced driver would drive after leaving the pub.
explanation: The only reliable way to ensure a safe drive home from a pub is to agree in advance on a designated driver who does not drink at all, since waiting an hour or trusting experience does not reliably remove alcohol's effects.

question: In order to avoid hitting a vehicle that makes a sudden stop in front of you:
answers: Keep your foot on the brake pedal so that you can also stop if needed.
Try to overtake it so it will be behind you.
Always keep sufficient distance from the vehicle in front .
Stop immediately upon noticing the brake lights of the vehicle in front, regardless of your distance from him.
explanation: Reacting to a sudden stop ahead requires enough space to brake within, so maintaining an adequate following distance at all times, rather than relying on watching brake lights, is what actually prevents a rear-end collision.

question: What is the difference between the two signs?
answers: Both signs belong to the group of obligatory signs and warn the driver of animals on the road.
Sign 146 warns of wild animals in the area. Sign 411 forbids the entry of animals harnessed or un-harnessed.
Both signs belong to the information group and warn the driver of animals on the road.
Sign 146 forbids the entry of animals harnessed or un-harnessed. 411 warns of wild animals on the road.
explanation: Sign 146 is a triangular warning sign alerting drivers that wild animals may cross the road ahead, while sign 411 is a prohibitory circular sign that legally bars any animal, led or loose, from entering that road.

question: Is a policeman permitted to stop a vehicle which is not lawfully loaded or marked?
answers: No, a policeman is not permitted to prohibit the vehicle from driving.
Yes, but only on an urban road.
No, a traffic policeman may only reprimand the vehicle owner, warn him and write him a ticket.
Yes, a policeman may prohibit the vehicle from driving until the freight is lawfully arranged.
explanation: Police enforcement authority over load safety includes the power to stop an unlawfully loaded or marked vehicle from continuing until the freight is properly secured or marked, since an unsafe load endangers other road users.

question: How should a driver conduct himself if one of his tires punctures while driving?
answers: Release his grip of the steering wheel and gradually brake the vehicle.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually brake the vehicle.
Release his grip of the steering wheel and strongly brake the vehicle.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and strongly brake the vehicle.
explanation: A tire blowout can pull the vehicle suddenly to one side, so keeping a firm grip on the wheel maintains directional control, while gradual, not sudden, braking avoids destabilizing the vehicle further.

question: When a driver is blinded by the sun, he should:
answers: Look as low as possible to the roadway, to avoid blinding.
Overtake the vehicle in front because it is better to drive on an open roadway.
Stay close to the vehicle in front, so it can block the sun for him.
Slow down in accordance with his range of vision and use the sunshade.
explanation: Sun glare reduces how far ahead a driver can actually see, so the safe response is to reduce speed to match that reduced visibility and use the sunshade to cut the glare, rather than trying to outrun it.

question: When is it permitted to drive in reverse?
answers: When it is required from a traffic-related point of view.
When it is required for personal reasons, even if driving in reverse is not essential.
Only when the roadway is wider than 4 meters.
It is always permitted, as long as we are always seen by other drivers.
explanation: Reversing is only permitted when a genuine traffic-related need for it exists, since driving backward severely limits the driver's field of view and control compared to driving forward.

question: When a continuous separation line is marked to your left, accompanied by a broken line to its left:
answers: You are permitted to cross the lines. However, vehicle traffic from the opposite direction is not permitted to cross them.
You are permitted to cross the lines. However, vehicle traffic from the opposite direction has right of way.
You are permitted to cross the lines because the driver has right of way.
You are forbidden to cross the lines. However, a vehicle from the opposite direction is permitted to cross them when the road is clear.
explanation: The rule for a continuous line paired with a broken line is that only the driver on the broken-line side may cross to overtake; since the continuous line is on your side, you may not cross, while the opposite driver may.

question: When the hand (parking) brake light on the dashboard is turned on while driving:
answers: It means that the handbrake is operated and should be released, because it activates the brakes.
It means that the handbrake is not operated and should be activated.
It means that the handbrake is ok. The light indicator is malfunctioning and should be replaced.
Everything is ok. It is a check light that should be on for as long as the handbrake is properly functioning.
explanation: The parking-brake warning light illuminates specifically when the handbrake is engaged, so seeing it lit while driving means the brake is still applying and must be released before continuing.

question: When a driver is blinded by the sun, he should:
answers: Drive faster until reaching a shaded place.
Slow down and adjust the driving speed to his current range of sight.
Look as low as possible to the roadway.
Overtake the vehicle in front because it is better to drive on an open roadway.
explanation: Being blinded by the sun temporarily reduces how much of the road a driver can see, so the correct response is to slow to a speed matching that reduced sight range rather than trying to drive through it at normal speed.

question: What are you required to do when during a night drive you are confronted with a vehicle that doesn’t dip its lights and blinds you?
answers: Slow down and keep as much as possible to the right.
Turn on the high beam to overcome the blinding effect of the other vehicle.
Drive faster to shorten the duration of being blinded.
Keep driving with a low beam at your current course and speed
explanation: When an oncoming driver fails to dip their lights, matching them with your own high beam only increases the glare for both drivers, so the safe response is to reduce speed and steer toward the right edge of your lane.

question: What is a driver required to do when the loading of the braking system’s air tanks takes longer than a reasonable time?
answers: Drive to a garage to repair the malfunction.
Reduce the engine’s RPM, to make the work of the compressor more efficient.
Check the system’s fuel filter and, if required, clean it.
Wait until the tanks are filled up, and ignore the problem.
explanation: An air braking system that takes longer than normal to build pressure signals a mechanical fault, such as a leak or failing compressor, which requires professional repair rather than a workaround.

question: What is the normal pressure in a vehicle’s pneumatic (compressed air) braking system?
answers: The maximum pressure the vehicle can generate.
As determined by the vehicle’s manufacturer.
The pressure in which the vehicle brakes efficiently.
As determined by local laws.
explanation: A pneumatic braking system's normal operating pressure is a design specification set by the vehicle's manufacturer, since it must match the specific brake hardware installed on that vehicle.

question: Is it permitted to drive a heavy vehicle when the air pressure in the braking system is below the required minimum?
answers: Yes, but only under permission of a policeman or an officer.
Yes, but only if the vehicle properly brakes.
Yes, if definitely no leak is detected.
No.
explanation: Driving with air pressure below the required minimum is never permitted, because the compressed-air braking system needs a minimum pressure threshold to guarantee full, reliable braking force.

question: Is it permitted to make changes in the vehicle’s design or type?
answers: The Owner of the vehicle is permitted to make changes in it as he pleases.
Yes, but provided that the owner of the vehicle notifies about it in advance and in writing to the vehicle’s manufacturer or agency.
Yes, but only if the change is made by a licensed garage.
Yes, but only with a written pre-approval of the Licensing Authority.
explanation: Any modification to a vehicle's design or type requires prior written approval from the Licensing Authority, since unapproved changes could compromise the vehicle's certified safety and roadworthiness.

question: Which sign warns of the presence of wild animals ahead?
explanation: Sign 146 is the triangular warning sign depicting an animal silhouette that alerts drivers to the possible presence of wild animals crossing the road ahead.

question: ?What road sign would be placed following sign 135 in the picture>
explanation: Sign 135 is the advance warning sign posted well before a pedestrian crossing, and it is followed closer to the crossing itself by sign 306, which specifically instructs drivers to give way to pedestrians on that crossing.

question: A “sidecar” is:
answers: A motorcycle with three wheels that are aligned one after the other.
A vehicle connected to the side of another vehicle with a bar that is not longer than 2.5 meters.
A fixture assembled on a wheel and connected to a motorcycle from the side, for the purpose of carrying a person or freight.
A vehicle driving next to another vehicle at the same speed.
explanation: A sidecar is legally defined by its structure and attachment, a wheeled fixture fastened to the side of a motorcycle to carry an extra person or cargo, not by speed, spacing, or the motorcycle's own wheel count.

question: Which sign denotes a lane for Cyclists only. Cycle in the direction of the arrow?
explanation: Road marking 804 is the painted line designating a bicycle lane, and cyclists using it are required to travel in the direction the lane's arrow indicates.

question: When driving behind a slow vehicle on a roadway while a continuous centre white line is marked to your left:
answers: You are only permitted to overtake if the slow vehicle is a non-motor one.
You are permitted to overtake if the vehicle in front drives slow for a long time
You are permitted to overtake, unless a prohibitory sign is placed.
You are permitted to overtake, providing you do not cross the continuous centre line..
explanation: A continuous center line prohibits crossing into the opposing lane, so overtaking a slow vehicle ahead is only legal if it can be done entirely within your own lane, without the maneuver requiring you to cross that solid line.

question: The speed limit for an commercial tractor (mule) on an inter-urban road is:
answers: According to the manufacturer’s manual.
According to road conditions and traffic signs.
explanation: Slow, low-powered vehicles such as tractors are limited to 40 km/h even on inter-urban roads, since their design and braking capability cannot safely handle higher highway speeds.

question: On an urban road, the speed limit for a 125cc or smaller motorcycle, with an engine power that doesn’t exceed 14.6 horse-powers (11 KW), unless indicated otherwise by any traffic sign, is:
explanation: On urban roads, the general speed limit of 50 km/h applies to small motorcycles up to 125cc/14.6 hp unless a sign specifically states otherwise, the same base limit that applies to cars in built-up areas.

question: Is a motorcycle permitted to tow other vehicles?
answers: Yes, but only during the dark and without endangering anyone
Yes.
No, a motor vehicle with 3 wheels or less is prohibited to tow.
Yes, when the towed vehicle is a two-wheeler.
explanation: Regulations bar any motor vehicle with three wheels or fewer, which includes motorcycles, from towing another vehicle, since such vehicles lack the stability and structural capacity for safe towing.

question: When is it required to turn-on the motorcycle’s headlights while driving?
answers: During daytime only, all the year round, on any type of road.
During the night only, on any type of road.
During light up time only.
Day and night, all the year round, on any type of road.
explanation: Regulation 97(b) requires a motorcycle's headlight and taillight to stay on at all times it is being ridden, day or night, on every type of road, unlike cars which only need lights during designated lighting time.

question: What are the vehicle’s control systems?
answers: Brakes, steering and accelerator.
Braking, steering and sound.
Steering, acceleration and air-conditioning.
Braking, steering and air-conditioning.
explanation: A vehicle's essential control systems are limited to braking, steering, and acceleration, which are the only inputs that actually change the vehicle's speed and direction; other systems play no role in vehicle control.

question: On a road designated for vehicle traffic, how is it required to stand a motorcycle with a sidecar during “light time” when the road is not lit?
answers: With the head light or parking light on.
With the brake light on.
With the rear light and parking lights on.
With only the parking light on.
explanation: When standing on a vehicle-traffic road during dark, unlit conditions, a motorcycle with a sidecar must keep its rear light and parking lights on so other drivers can see the stationary vehicle from a distance.

question: In an automatic gearbox, what is a driver required to do before shifting from the P gear to any other gear?
answers: Apply the brakes firmly.
Step firmly on the accelerator.
Step firmly on the clutch pedal.
Step on the brake and the clutch pedals simultaneously. And then shift to the required gear.
explanation: Before shifting an automatic gearbox out of Park, the vehicle must be held stationary by firmly applying the brakes, since Park alone should not be relied on to prevent unwanted movement during the gear change.

question: Under what condition is it permitted to drive a motorcycle?
answers: Wearing a standard helmet that is secured to the rider’s head and will not fall-off whist driving.
The motorcyclist should have a rescue kit in case of an accident.
The motorcyclist should ensure that the fuel tank is full and secured before beginning to drive.
The rider must wear a helmet, even if it is not secured to the rider’s head.
explanation: Motorcycle riding is only permitted while wearing an approved helmet that is properly fastened so it cannot come off during riding, since an unsecured helmet gives no real head protection in a fall or collision.

question: What driving license class is required for driving a work vehicle that tows a trailer with an all up weight exceeding 4,000 kg?
answers: B.
C+E.
A.
D.
explanation: Towing a trailer whose gross weight exceeds 4,000 kg behind a work vehicle requires a combined C+E license class, since this combination exceeds the towing limits covered by a basic work-vehicle or car license.

question: What is the minimum age requirement for carrying another passenger on a motorcycle?
answers: 18 yrs.
16 yrs.
Age is of no significance.
explanation: A motorcyclist must be at least 18 years old before being permitted to carry a passenger, reflecting the added riding skill and judgment needed to safely carry another person.

question: How many passengers, besides the driver, is it permitted to carry on a motorcycle and a motorctcle with sidecar?
answers: The number of passengers indicated in the driving license.
The number of passengers indicated in the motorcycle’s insurance policy.
The number of passengers approved by the Licensing Authority noted on the vehicle’s registration document.
As the number of seats suitable for additional riders.
explanation: The legal limit on passengers a motorcycle or sidecar may carry is the number specifically approved by the Licensing Authority and recorded on the vehicle's registration document, not a number set by insurance or seating alone.

question: How should an additional passenger sit on a motorcycle?
answers: The passenger should sit with both legs on the right side of the motorcycle.
The passenger should sit with both legs on the left side of the motorcycle.
The passenger should sit astride the motorcycle with his feet supported by the foot pedals..
The passenger can sit on the motorcycle however he chooses to.
explanation: A pillion passenger must sit astride the seat with both feet resting on the foot pegs, since this position keeps the passenger balanced and prevents legs from dragging or catching on the road or wheel.

question: Is a two-wheeler permitted to drive at the side of another two-wheeler?
answers: Absolutely not.
Yes, always.
No, except for the purpose of overtaking or bypassing another vehicle only.
Yes, but only on an urban road.
explanation: Two-wheeled vehicles are required to ride in single file, and are only permitted to draw level with another two-wheeler momentarily while actually completing an overtaking or bypassing maneuver.

question: Is a motorcyclist permitted to park in a bus station?
answers: It is prohibited to park within a distance of 12 meters before the station and 15 meters after it.
Yes, if he parks the motorcycle on the sidewalk.
It is prohibited to park within the limits of a marked bus station.
Yes, if he parks the motorcycle in parallel to the sidewalk.
explanation: A marked bus station is a no-parking zone for all vehicles, including motorcycles, so parking anywhere within its marked limits is prohibited regardless of how the motorcycle is positioned.

question: What is the risk of driving a motorcycle while its kick-stand is down?
answers: Damage would be caused to the roadway and other infrastructures.
The motorcycle would be unbalanced.
The kick-stand will hit the roadway and might cause the motorcycle to roll-over.
The kick-stand would wear out and cause the motorcycle to fall.
explanation: Riding with the kick-stand still extended risks the stand striking the road surface, especially while leaning into a turn, which can catch and throw the motorcycle off balance and cause it to roll over.

question: A motorcyclist should not carry on the motorcycle a package, bundle or object:
answers: That would prevent him from having full control of the motorcycle.
That is not wrapped as required.
That sticks out beyond the motorcycle’s rear.
That would prevent him from sitting comfortably on the motorcycle.
explanation: The overriding safety principle for carrying anything on a motorcycle is that it must never interfere with the rider's ability to fully control the machine, since loss of control is what actually causes a crash.

question: What is the minimum time requirement of having a driving license in order to drive a tractor with an own weight exceeding 3,200 kg, or that is joined with a trailer that has an all up weight exceeding 4,000 kg?
