answers: Two years from the date of obtaining a tractor driving license.
6 months from the date of obtaining a tractor driving license.
3 months from the date of obtaining a tractor driving license.
One year from the date of obtaining a tractor driving license.
explanation: New tractor-license holders must wait 6 months of experience before being permitted to drive a heavier tractor or one towing a trailer over 4,000 kg, giving them time to build basic handling skill first.

question: The license class that is required for riding a 125cc or smaller motorcycle with an engine power of up to 14.6 horse-powers (11 KW) is:
answers: B.
D.
explanation: Under Israel's graduated motorcycle licensing, the entry-level Class A2 covers the smallest motorcycles, 125cc or less with power up to 14.6 hp (11 kW), which is why this power range requires an A2 license.

question: The license class that is required for riding a motorcycle with an engine power of up to 33 horse-powers (25 KW) is:
answers: C.
D.
explanation: The next tier up in Israel's graduated motorcycle licensing, Class A1, covers motorcycles with power up to 33 hp (25 kW), sitting between the entry-level A2 class and the unrestricted A class.

question: The license class that is required for driving a motorcycle with an engine power of more than 33 horse-powers (25 KW) is:
answers: A.
B.
explanation: Once a motorcycle's engine power exceeds 33 hp (25 kW), it falls outside the limits of both the A2 and A1 classes, requiring the unrestricted Class A license.

question: What is the minimum age requirement for obtaining a Class A2 driving license?
answers: 18 yrs, subject to written consent of a parent or a guardian.
14 yrs, subject to written consent of a parent or a guardian.
20 yrs, subject to written consent of a parent or a guardian.
16 yrs, subject to written consent of a parent or a guardian.
explanation: Class A2, the entry-level motorcycle license, can be obtained at age 16, but because the applicant is a minor, the law requires the written consent of a parent or guardian.

question: When a rider cries a pillion passanger the law obliges:
answers: The passenger feet will be on the foot support at all times.
The pillion rider will hold the hips of the rider all times.
The pillion passnger will be a least 8 years old.
Both the passengers legs will be on the right side of the motorcycle.
explanation: The law requires a pillion passenger to keep both feet on the foot supports throughout the ride, since this keeps the passenger's weight balanced and their legs clear of the wheels and road.

question: What is special about the operation of the motorcycle’s brakes?
answers: The rear and front brakes can be operated separately.
Brakes operation is safer in a motorcycle because it is done with the hands only.
In a motorcycle you cannot brake every wheel separately.
The motorcycle can brake at any speed on the spot.
explanation: Unlike a car's single brake pedal that applies all wheel brakes together, a motorcycle has independent controls, a hand lever for the front brake and a foot pedal for the rear, letting the rider operate each separately.

question: What is a reasonable and safe motorcycle riding speed?
answers: The speed in which the rider exceeds the motorcycle’s driving limits or the road’s designated speed limit.
The statutory speed limit.
It depends on the motorcycle’s mechanical condition, age and safety systems.
A speed in which the rider can identify all road details and in which he has full control of the motorcycle.
explanation: A reasonable and safe riding speed, consistent with the general reasonable-speed principle, is one slow enough that the rider can perceive every relevant road detail and still keep full control of the motorcycle.

question: When visibility conditions are impaired:
answers: Stay close to the vehicle in front, to be assisted by its lights.
Keep to the right of the road and drive faster until visibility conditions improve.
Drive slower and maintain a wider gap from the vehicle in front.
Maintain normal speed, but remain constantly alert in case an emergency brake is required.
explanation: When visibility is impaired, both the driver's sight distance and reaction margin shrink, so the correct response is to reduce speed and increase the following gap, giving more time and space to react to hazards.

question: Why is it important to have a wide field of vision through the helmet?
answers: To allow people with poor eyesight to drive motorcycles as well.
To determine safety distances and driving speed and to reduce response times.
To increase motorcycle control in urban roads.
To prevent tiredness on long rides during the day and especially during the night.
explanation: A wide field of view through the helmet lets a rider take in more of the surrounding road environment, which is what allows them to judge a safe following distance and speed, and notice hazards sooner, shortening response time.

question: What is the factor that affects the rider’s ability to brake, swerve or accelerate the motorcycle?
answers: The motorcycle’s grip on the road.
The rider’s standard clothing.
The rider’s weight.
The motorcycle seat design.
explanation: Braking, swerving, and accelerating are all ultimately limited by how much traction the tires have with the road surface, since every one of those actions depends on the tires transmitting force to the ground without sliding.

question: What is the problem in detecting an obstacle before a motorcycle at a very late stage?
answers: The time left for responding and braking is too short.
The obstacle’s weight can not be precisely evaluated.
There is no problem in late detection of an obstacle.
There is not enough time to change gears.
explanation: Since a motorcycle's stopping ability depends on reaction time plus braking distance, detecting a hazard too late leaves too little time and distance to brake before reaching it, making late detection genuinely dangerous.

question: How does road-marking paint affect the motorcycle?
answers: The paint might be smoother than the roadway itself and might cause skidding.
The motorcycle tires spoil the roadway-marking paint.
The white color on the roadway might blind and mislead the motorcyclist.
The paint significantly impairs the life span of the motorcycle’s tires.
explanation: Painted road markings are typically smoother than the surrounding asphalt, so they offer noticeably less grip, especially when wet, and can make a motorcycle's tires skid if braking or leaning is done on them.

question: Apart from legal demand, why should a motorcyclist avoid driving in the center of the lane?
answers: Because it annoys car drivers
Because the center of the lane is the dirtiest and most greasy part of a road.
He is not prohibited from driving in the center of a two-way roadway, or in the center of a marked lane within a two way roadway.
Because he should keep to the left and take account of other riders.
explanation: Oil, grease, and fluid drips from vehicles accumulate mostly in the center of the lane, so riding there reduces tire traction quite apart from any legal rule about lane position.

question: How would you drive your motorcycle when you are forced to cross an oil slick on the road?
answers: Slow down gently using the front brake during the entire time of crossing.
Slow down gently using the rear brake during the entire time of crossing.
Keep driving straight ahead without braking or accelerating and squeeze the clutch operating lever.
Slow down sharply with an even distribution between the rear and front brakes, until you pass the oil slick.
explanation: On an oil slick a motorcycle needs maximum, evenly distributed traction, so the rider should hold a straight line without braking or accelerating and pull in the clutch to remove drivetrain influence on the wheels until clear.

question: How should a motorcyclist cross an oil slick on the road?
answers: Continue driving fast.
Brake strongly with both brakes.
Drive straight without braking.
Drive straight, accelerate and cross the stain quickly.
explanation: Braking or swerving on a slippery patch can easily break traction, so the safest technique is to keep the motorcycle upright and moving straight through it without touching the brakes.

question: How would you operate the motorcycle while crossing an oil slick on the road?
answers: Lean backwards and improve braking by shifting the weight to the rear wheel.
Accelerate and cross the stain as quickly as possible an in a straight line.
Release the gas handle and the brakes and press the clutch handle.
Bend forward and improve steering by shifting the driver’s weight to the front wheel.
explanation: Releasing the throttle and brakes and pulling in the clutch removes any accelerating or braking force on the tires, letting the motorcycle coast through the low-traction patch with the best chance of keeping its grip.

question: Which number marks the length of the “rear extension” of the bus in the picture?
explanation: This vehicle-dimension diagram labels the rear overhang, the distance the body extends behind the rear axle, and the number keyed to that measurement in the picture is 78, which the question is testing the ability to read.

question: How will a dirty front lamp influence night driving?
answers: It will affect the field of vision.
The field of vision will grow.
It will cause a dazzeling (blinding).
Dirt will have no affect on the rider ability to recognize problems.
explanation: A dirty headlight lens scatters and blocks light output, so it directly shortens the distance the beam actually illuminates, cutting down the rider's field of vision at night.

question: What are the main factors affecting the motorcyclist’s ability to detect obstacles on the road?
answers: Traffic conditions around the motorcycle.
The proper functioning of the brakes and the tires.
The motorcycle’s mechanical condition.
The motorcyclist’s riding skill and sitting position.
explanation: How well a motorcyclist scans and reads the road for hazards depends heavily on riding skill and posture, since an alert, well-positioned rider spots developing dangers earlier than one relying only on the bike's mechanical condition.

question: It is not permitted to carry a passenger on a motorcycle unless:
answers: The passenger wears a crash helmet as well as knee and elbow protectors.
The driver wears a crash helmet – the passenger doesn’t have to do so.
The driver and the passenger wear crash helmets.
The passenger holds a valid motorcycle driver’s license.
explanation: Israeli traffic regulations require both the rider and any passenger on a motorcycle to wear a crash helmet before a passenger may legally be carried.

question: Why is it that the control of a motorcycle is decreased while entering a turn?
answers: Because the motorcycle is decelerating during the entire course of the turn.
Because the rider’s position is lower than usual.
Because less surface of the tyre maintains contact on the road when the driver leans the motorcycle over.
Because it needs to accelerate during the entire course of the turn.
explanation: Leaning a motorcycle into a turn tilts the tire so a smaller portion of its tread stays flat on the road, shrinking the contact patch and the traction margin available for steering and braking.

question: What effect does a curve or a turn have on the motorcycle’s ability to brake?
answers: It has no effect on the motorcycle’s ability to brake.
It requires the driver to slow down before the curve or the turn and to brake very gently.
The driver’s response time is doubled during turns or curves.
During a curve or a turn only the rear brake can be used and therefore braking is impaired.
explanation: Because braking hard while leaned over can easily break traction, the safe technique is to complete most of the slowing down before entering the curve and use only very gentle braking, if any, once turning.

question: A  passenger is not permitted on a motorcycle unless:
answers: A permit is given by the motorcycle’s manufacturer.
it is listed on the vehicle’s license .
He is listed in the insurance policy.
A permit is given by the vehicle’s importer.
explanation: A motorcycle may only carry a passenger if the vehicle's registration document (license) specifically records it as approved for a passenger.

question: In which direction should a motorcyclist focus his sight when entering into a turn?
answers: Far ahead.
In the direction of the turn and the direction of its exit.
As close to the motorcycle as possible.
He should look far ahead and concentrate on the road signs and the surroundings of the turn.
explanation: Looking through the turn toward its exit lets the rider naturally steer along the intended path, a standard technique since a motorcycle tends to follow where the eyes are pointed.

question: Why do we have to lean the motorcycle while turning?
answers: To lesser the effect of the centrifugal force (a force acting on the motorcycle whilst turning).
To improve tire grip on a dry or wet roadway.
To completely annul the effect of the centrifugal force.
To improve our field of vision and our ability to respond to surprises on the road.
explanation: Leaning the motorcycle shifts its balance so that the combined weight and centrifugal force line up through the tire contact patch, counteracting the outward centrifugal force generated in the turn.

question: How should we react to the centrifugal force created while the motorcycle turns?
answers: Accelerate upon entering the turn and slowing down when coming out of it.
Accelerate strongly before the turn, in order to cancel the centrifugal force.
Lean the motorcycle into the turn.
Brake intermittently.
explanation: Leaning the motorcycle into the turn is how a rider counteracts the outward-pulling centrifugal force and keeps the combined forces balanced through the tires.

question: Is a motorcyclist permitted to cross a sidewalk?
answers: Yes, but only to bypass an obstacle on the road.
Yes, but only to drop a passenger.
Yes, in order to enter a yard or a garage.
Yes, but only to pick up a passenger.
explanation: Crossing a sidewalk is only permitted at the point needed to enter a private yard or garage, not as a general shortcut or for picking up or dropping off passengers.

question: What would be the result of sharply braking a motorcycle while turning?
answers: The motorcycle will drive faster.
Sliding of the rear wheel.
The front wheel would be lifted in the air.
Sliding of the front wheel.
explanation: Braking sharply mid-turn overloads the already-reduced rear tire contact patch caused by the lean angle, which typically breaks traction and slides the rear wheel out.

question: How should you conduct yourself when detecting an oily and slippery area on the roadway while making a turn?
answers: You should always try to straighten the motorcycle as much as possible, even if you swerve from your lane as a result.
Brake sharply with both brakes and avoid brake-lock.
Accelerate to improve the road grip of the tires.
You should brake sharply even after entering the slippery area. At such a situation you have nothing to lose.
explanation: Straightening the motorcycle as much as possible maximizes the tire's contact patch and grip on a slippery patch, which takes priority even if it means momentarily crossing outside the lane.

question: How would you, while driving a motorcycle, evade an obstacle – such as an object that is laid on the road – that suddenly appears in front of you?
answers: Brake before the obstacle and while on it. This way you ensure maximum braking time.
Substantially accelerate the motorcycle to maintain balance.
Brake before the obstacle and then ease-off the brakes just before it and evade it.
Drive faster and pass the obstacle without any delay.
explanation: Because a motorcycle cannot brake hard and swerve at the same time without risking loss of control, braking must be finished and eased off just before the obstacle so the rider can then steer around it.

question: What maintenance work is required on a motorcycle?
answers: Motorcycle periodic treatment is only required before its annual test.
In a new motorcycle there is no need to perform regular treatments.
A periodic treatment according to the instructions of the garage manager. He knows the motorcycle best.
A periodic service according to the manufacturer’s manual.
explanation: Motorcycles should be serviced on the schedule set out in the manufacturer's manual, since that schedule is calibrated to the specific machine rather than to informal judgment or only the annual test.

question: According to the law, while driving at night and in good weather conditions – what is the minimal distance that should be covered by the vehicle’s headlights?
answers: The range of the headlights is not defined by law, and it is determined at the discretion of the vehicle’s manufacturer.
100 meters for the high beam, and 30 meters for the low(dipped) beam.
120 meters for the high beam, and 50 meters for the low beam.
150 meters for the high beam, and 60 meters for the low beam.
explanation: Traffic regulations set minimum illumination distances for vehicle headlights at night — 100 meters for high beam and 30 meters for low beam — so a driver can see and stop within the lit range.

question: How would we create an efficient safety space in our front, rear and to the side whilst riding in traffic??
answers: By positioning ourselves in the middle of the road and driving fast.
By choosing the proper driving lane and speed in relation to the traffic condition around us.
By signaling other vehicles to keep away.
By keeping to the right of the road or of the lane and driving fast.
explanation: An effective safety cushion around a motorcycle comes from actively choosing the right lane position and speed for the traffic conditions at hand, not from a fixed position or simply driving fast.

question: Why is it required to keep a distance from our front, rear and sides?
answers: To limit our field of vision and our ability to use the “hard shoulder”.
To avoid smoke and dirt from other vehicles.
To allow other two-wheelers to safely merge with traffic.
To ensure response time and space to avoid threats from other vehicles.
explanation: Keeping distance to the front, rear, and sides gives a rider the reaction time and physical space needed to respond safely if a nearby vehicle suddenly creates a hazard.

question: Does an agricultural trailer require a warning triangle?
answers: Only trailers with an own weight of up to 4,000 kg.
No.
Only small trailers with an own weight of up to 500 kg.
Yes.
explanation: Israeli law requires a warning triangle to be carried in vehicles including agricultural trailers, so it can be placed on the road if the vehicle breaks down or stops unexpectedly.

question: Who is responsible for keeping a safety distance from the front, rear and sides while riding a motorcycle amongst other vehicle?
answers: The other drivers around.
The motorcyclist only.
The infrastructure-planning authorities.
The Police and the Traffic Police.
explanation: The duty to keep a safe distance from surrounding traffic rests on the motorcyclist himself; he cannot rely on other drivers to maintain that space for him.

question: What is the most important measure a motorcyclist can take while driving besides or nearby other vehicles?
answers: Adjust his speed to the speed of the vehicles around him – even if it exceeds speed limit.
Pay strict attention to the movements of other vehicles in good time.
Reduce his response space and distance.
Ride with legs close to the ground to improve stability.
explanation: Closely watching how nearby vehicles are behaving lets a rider spot early warning signs of a developing hazard, which is a more effective defensive measure than matching their speed or accepting less following distance.

question: Is a tractor driver permitted to cross a sidewalk?
answers: Yes, to pick up a passenger.
Yes, in order to enter a yard or a garage.
Yes, to drop a passenger.
Yes, to bypass an obstacle on the road.
explanation: A tractor, like other vehicles, may cross a sidewalk only at the point needed to enter a yard or garage, not to pick up or drop off passengers.

question: If a rider feels that the motorcycle foot brake,does not work efficently he should:
answers: Stop the motorcycle and immediately repair the fault.
Take some air out of the wheels to overcome the malfunction.
Change between the front and rear wheels.
Stop at the next gas station and increase tire air pressure.
explanation: A foot brake that isn't working properly is a serious safety defect, so the rider must stop and have it repaired immediately rather than continue riding or try to compensate with tire pressure changes.

question: How is a motorcyclist required to overtake another vehicle?
answers: As fast as possible, even if it means to exceed speed limit for a brief moment.
From the right side of the overtaken vehicle, and as close as possible to it.
From the left side of the overtaken vehicle, while keeping a proper side distance from it.
In a manner that allows him to always see the other vehicle in both mirrors.
explanation: Overtaking must be done from the left of the vehicle being passed while keeping an adequate side clearance, which is the standard rule for passing safely rather than crowding the other vehicle.

question: When are you (a motorcycle rider) required to return to your driving lane at the end of overtaking?
answers: After first glancing in the mirrors and then making another check by looking briefly backwards over your right shoulder.
A reasonable time after passing the overtaken vehicle.
After seeing the overtaken vehicle in both motorcycle mirrors.
When riding a motorcycle, you are not required to return to your former driving lane.
explanation: Because mirrors leave blind spots a motorcyclist can't fully trust, the safe way to rejoin the lane after overtaking is to check the mirrors and then confirm with a quick glance back over the shoulder before moving over.

question: Is it permitted to ride a motorcycle in which the silencer was removed from the exhaust?
answers: Yes, but only on a non-urban road.
Absolutely not.
Yes, but only on a freeway.
Yes,
explanation: Riding a motorcycle with the silencer removed from the exhaust is not permitted under any circumstances, since it is a listed vehicle-condition violation regardless of the type of road.

question: The main factors affecting a motor cycle riders ability to identify obstacles on the road are:
answers: The motorcycle’s mechanical condition.
The motorcycle’s size.
The proper function of the brakes and tires.
The motorcycle’s position on the road and in traffic.
explanation: A motorcyclist's ability to spot obstacles in time depends heavily on where the bike is positioned within the lane and relative to surrounding traffic, since that position determines the rider's actual sightlines.

question: The main factors affecting a motorcyclist’s ability to try and evade objects that fall from a vehicle in front are:
answers: The motorcycle’s mechanical condition.
Excessive air pressure in the motorcycle’s tires – double the required pressure,
The proper function of the brakes and tires.
Keeping distance and maintaining an effective field of vision at all times.
explanation: Keeping adequate distance from the vehicle ahead and maintaining a clear, active field of vision are what actually give a rider the time and visibility needed to react to an object falling from that vehicle.

question: Is a motorcyclist permitted to drive on the sidewalk?
answers: Yes, as long as pedestrians are not disturbed by it.
Yes, in order to cross it and enter premises.
Never.
Yes, when road traffic is congested.
explanation: A motorcyclist may only ride briefly onto a sidewalk to cross it while entering adjoining premises, not to travel along it or bypass traffic.

question: Driver of a commercial vehicle with an all up weight exceeding 6,000 kg, shall have a rest without working of at least 25 consecutive hours during every period of:
answers: 6 days.
12 days.
8 days.
10 days.
explanation: Regulations governing commercial drivers of heavy vehicles require a rest period of at least 25 consecutive hours within every 8-day cycle, to limit fatigue-related risk.

question: Which number marks the length of the “rear extension” of this vehicle?

question: Which sign permits a vehicle driver or a Tram driver to proceed only to the right?
explanation: Traffic signal 711 is the directional signal used to indicate that vehicle and tram drivers may proceed only to the right at that point, distinguishing it from the other numbered signals in that series.

question: What risk do riders of two-wheelers face while passing between two rows of cars that stand before an intersection?
answers: There is no risk, as there is always enough space for two-wheelers to pass comfortably and safely.
The risk is that at the beginning of the row, next to the intersection, there is no more space left because there are many two-wheelers standing there.
They might hit pedestrians who are not using a regulated pedestrian crossing.
They might be hit by cigarette butts thrown by vehicle drivers.
explanation: Pedestrians sometimes step out between queued cars away from a marked, regulated crossing, and a filtering motorcyclist's limited sightlines between the rows make that a real collision risk.

question: What risk do riders of two-wheelers face while passing between two rows of moving cars before an intersection?
answers: Being hit by a car that suddenly swerves from its lane to the passage in which the motorcycle is proceeding.
There is no risk, as there is always enough space for two-wheelers to pass comfortably and safely.
The rider might scare drivers who are short-tempered anyway.
The risk is that at the beginning of the row, next to the intersection, there is no more space left because there are many two-wheelers standing there.
explanation: A driver in a stopped or slow-moving row may suddenly change lanes into the gap a motorcyclist is using to filter through, often without checking mirrors or blind spots for a bike there.

question: When a driving license includes certain restrictions:
answers: These restrictions concern the motorcycle’s standard and not the manner of riding it.
The driver must obey these restrictions.
The restriction is just a recommendation which doesn’t obligate the driver.
The driver shall decide at his own discretion which restrictions should be taken into consideration.
explanation: Restrictions noted on a driving license are legally binding conditions the driver must follow, not optional guidance the driver can choose to ignore.

question: Is a motorcyclist permitted to drive on a marked pedestrian path?
answers: No..
Yes, if the path leads to a vehicle parking lot.
No, unless the roadway next to the path is blocked by vehicles.
Yes, if there are no Pedestrians on the path.
explanation: A motorcyclist, like any motor vehicle, is not permitted to ride on a marked pedestrian path, which is reserved for pedestrian safety.

question: What basic equipment and clothing are required for a safe ride?
answers: Full helmet, rigid-cloth pants, high shoes, gloves and a basic riding jacket.
Half helmet, long trousers, shoes, gloves, a basic riding jacket and a back belt.
Full helmet, safety goggles, pants, sandals and a basic riding jacket with body protectors.
Half helmet, safety goggles, pants, shoes and a basic riding jacket with shoulder and elbow protectors.
explanation: Full head protection along with abrasion-resistant pants, sturdy high shoes, gloves, and a proper riding jacket form the recommended minimum protective gear for safe motorcycle riding.

question: Is it obligatory to install a mirror on a motorcycle?
answers: No, except for motorcycles and a side-car.
Yes, it is lawfully required on all types of motorcycles.
No, the driver can decide at his own discretion whether or not to install a mirror.
Yes, but only on motorcycles with a sidecar.
explanation: Israeli traffic law requires every motorcycle, regardless of type, to be fitted with at least one mirror; it is not left to the rider's discretion.

question: What considerations are taken into account in choosing a motorcycle helmet?
answers: The helmet strength is of no significance. The most important is that it fits the size and shape of the rider’s head.
The helmet doesn’t have to be standard, but it should have an aerodynamic design, to reduce fuel consumption.
The helmet should have a good ventilation system and as many fastening straps as possible.
The helmet should be standard, provide full protection (also to the chin) and fit the size and shape of the rider’s head.
explanation: A proper motorcycle helmet must meet the required safety standard, protect the chin as a full-face design does, and fit the rider's head correctly, since strength and fit both matter for real protection.

question: Continuous braking on a winding descent can cause:
answers: Over heating and weaker braking than normal.
Over heating and stronger braking than normal.
Cooling of the breaks and weak braking.
Continuous braking has no negative affect.
explanation: Continuous braking on a long winding descent overheats the brake components, which reduces friction and produces weaker braking than normal — a phenomenon known as brake fade.

question: How would you choose appropriate shoes for riding a motorcycle?
answers: You should choose high shoes made from a friction-resistant fiber material.
You should choose light and comfortable shoes enabling flexible riding.
You should choose high insulated shoes.
There are no rules to it: Any shoe or sandal is proper for the motorcycle’s safe operation.
explanation: High boots made of abrasion- and friction-resistant material protect the foot and ankle and keep their grip on the footpegs, unlike light shoes or sandals.

question: Where on the motorcycle is it recommended to place luggage, so that its impact on the motorcycle’s stability is minimal?
answers: Close to the rear end of the motorcycle and as high as possible.
Close to the front end of the motorcycle and as high as possible.
Close to the center of the motorcycle and as low as possible, so that the luggage doesn’t stick out from the front or rear.
Close to the rear end of the motorcycle and as low as possible, so that the luggage doesn’t stick out from the rear.
explanation: Placing luggage close to the motorcycle's center of gravity and as low as possible, without it sticking out front or rear, minimizes its effect on the bike's balance and handling.

question: What is the danger of riding a motorcycle on a wet roadway?
answers: Motorcycle skidding and roll-over, the lower the speed is.
The penetration of water into the engine, which creates rust.
Motorcycle skidding and roll-over, the greater the speed is.
Motorcycle roll-over if the driver presses the clutch handle abruptly.
explanation: On a wet road a motorcycle's tires lose grip more severely the faster it is going, so the risk of skidding and rolling over rises with speed rather than falling.

question: An additional passenger is not permitted on an A.T.V, unless:
answers: It is indicated in the insurance policy.
It is indicated in the driver’s license.
A permit is given by the vehicle’s importer.
It is indicated in the vehicle’s registration document.
explanation: An ATV may only carry an additional passenger if that is specifically indicated in the vehicle's registration document, the same principle applied to motorcycle passengers.

question: Is it permitted for a motorcycle owner to replace the motorcycle’s original-size tires with tires of a different size?
answers: Yes, but only on motorcycles with a sidecar.
No, unless he obtains a pre-approval to do so from the Licensing Authority.
Yes, provided that the new size deviates within 10% of the size indicated in the vehicle’s registration document.
Yes, he may save fuel that way.
explanation: Changing to tires of a different size than shown in the vehicle's registration document is not allowed unless the Licensing Authority grants prior approval, since it affects the vehicle's approved specifications.

question: What is the statutory length limit of the vehicle in the picture?
